t: Royal Commission: no campaign file, no demolition letters
x: The Royal Commission (RCAHMW, RC26-0375) replied that its registered files hold no letters or records about Tŷ Mawr Farm, Llandough, including any correspondence between C.N. Johns and Mrs Buckler or on the circumstances of the demolition; its holdings are limited to the Coflein archive items (NPRN 20182), and aerial-photograph searches would be chargeable.

t: Registration certificate of “undisputed possession”
x: Compulsory registration of title began in the Vale of Glamorgan on 1 Dec 1975. The solicitor’s certificate form for a first registration states belief that the applicant “is and has been in undisputed possession or in receipt of rents and profits” and knows of nothing “adverse to the applicant”. The February 1983 wording itself is unseen.

t: Western Ground Rents papers passed between companies
x: Glamorgan Archives D696 holds Western Ground Rents records of 1938–44, which “ended up in the custody of Capital Law after being transferred to various companies who purchased the leaseholds”; “the leaseholds were later taken over by the British Petroleum Pensions Trust”. Whether Llandough appears in them is not established.

t: NPCC internal reviews: no records on 1988 operation
x: On 29 September 2026 the National Police Chiefs’ Council upheld its FOI 3156/2026 answer on review (3176/2026): it held no recorded information on the transfer, archiving, retention, disposal or location of the relevant historical records. Review 3157/2026 upheld that an earlier request was not a valid FOI request.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R50 — NPCC internal reviews 3157/2026 and 3176/2026 (29 September 2026)

t: 1824 Bute survey: Cedfin or Ty Mawr tenanted
x: David Stewart’s 1824 survey of the Bute Glamorgan estates (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1) recorded plan 19, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, Llandough: 139a 3r 8p including about 20 acres of wood, let to “John Gedrick Tent.”, with land of the “Late Thos. Williams” added. The tenant’s name reading needs the archive image.

t: 1974 architectural survey of the house
x: H. J. Thomas’s 1974 survey and floor plan, held by RCAHMW (National Monuments Record), documented a sub-medieval or late-seventeenth-century building. RCAHMW records that the house was only partly recorded because of the ownership dispute. The related Johns–Buckler correspondence has been lost “since 1986/87”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E137 — 1974 H. J. Thomas architectural survey and floor plan (RCAHMW / National Monuments Record)

t: Housing application on former Great House Farm site
x: A planning officer’s report on an outline application for residential development and a new access road described “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church … The site formerly contained a number of buildings including Great House Farm, but all buildings on the site have now been demolished.”

t: High Court fight ends; BP acts “within hours”
x: The South Wales Echo of 6 December 1988 reported that the family’s battle of “more than 30 years to prove they owned the historic farmhouse” ended the previous afternoon in the High Court in Cardiff, and that “within hours” BP Properties acted; the farmhouse was demolished in the early hours of 6 December.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-07 — South Wales Echo search extract, Tuesday 6 December 1988

t: Cadw lists a Rhoose farmhouse unseen inside, 1988
x: On 12 Oct 1988 Cadw listed Lower Farmhouse, Rhoose (record 13428), “as a little altered early C19 farmhouse having group value with the adjoining cottage”, noting “Interior not available at resurvey”. The record shows the bar applied to a comparable Vale farmhouse weeks before Great House was demolished.

t: Echo prints “rent free” framing on eviction day
x: On 29 April 1988, the day of the eviction attempt, the South Wales Echo printed that the dispute had “been waged for two generations”, that Mr Buckler’s mother had lost “three previous High Court cases”, and that “in 1974 BP Properties agreed to allow Mrs Buckler to remain in the farmhouse rent free”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-01 — Friday 29 April 1988: South Wales Echo (British Newspaper Archive extract)

t: 1987: council drops farm right-of-way application
x: Llandough Community Council minutes of 1987 record “RIGHT OF WAY FROM GREAT HOUSE FARM TO THE SWISS COTTAGES … there is no justification for the right of way being submitted … no further action.” The minutes name Debenham Tewson as “the agents for BP Properties” and record a licence fee paid to them.

t: Branwen’s recollection of the 1988 removal
x: Branwen recalled in September 2026 that she went to the farm during the 1988 removal to fetch medicine from the house, not to serve the writ as ITV presented it. She stated that men who appeared to be soldiers dragged her, kicked her and threw her over the gate; ITV footage shows her arm in a sling.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E114 — Branwen: September 2026 recollection of the 1988 removal

t: BP Pension Fund sells Llandough and Leckwith woods
x: South Wales Echo reports of 1989–90 recorded that woodland was “sold to the LAW by BP Pension Fund which owned it until 1988”, including seven woods “in Llandough and Leckwith”, among them Coed Cwm Cydfin, and that the Land Authority for Wales advertised Llandough “Prime Residential Building Land”.

t: Cadw: only two 1988 photographs held
x: Welsh Government/Cadw answered ATISN 27021 on 11 June 2026: “the house was visited and assessed for listing by Cadw inspectors and did not meet the listing criteria. As such, the only record of the inspection we hold are the two photographs enclosed.” No written listing assessment was produced.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R37-A1 — Welsh Government/Cadw ATISN 27021 response letter, 11 June 2026

t: Strasbourg application 14464/88 declared inadmissible
x: William Buckler’s application 14464/88 to the European Commission of Human Rights (lodged 3 May 1988) was declared inadmissible on 14 April 1989: no “possession” because the courts had held the property belonged to another. The case file was later destroyed under the Court’s retention policy.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E145 — European Commission of Human Rights application 14464/88 and the 14 April 1989 inadmissibility decision

t: Marconi’s wireless trials at Lavernock, 1897
x: A Cardiff newspaper column of May 1897 reported Guglielmo Marconi’s wireless telegraphy trials between Lavernock Point and Flat Holm, witnessed by the Post Office’s engineer-in-chief. The Glamorgan Village Book records that Marconi slept at Great House Farm while working on these experiments.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N02 — 1897: “Wireless Telegraphy. Marconi Invention Tested at Lavernock”

t: Glamorgan Village Book on Great House Farm
x: The Glamorgan Village Book’s Llandough page records that visitors to the farm saw how people “made their butter, cheese and beer”, “cheese drying rooms hollowed out of a solid wall”, the bedroom where “monks took rest on their travels”, and that “Marconi too slept here in a four poster bed”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E110-A5 — The Glamorgan Village Book: Llandough page

t: Medieval rowel spur found at Llandough, 1858
x: Museum Wales object 63.24/1, a 14th–15th-century iron rowel spur, was found in 1858 at Llandough Church Farm with six male skeletons during building work. It was displayed in the Museum’s “Origins” gallery until 2014. The record was released with the Museum’s FOI reply on 5 October 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33-A2 — Museum Wales collections record 63.24/1: medieval iron rowel spur, Llandough Church Farm, 1858

t: 1980 talk: Roman villa, medieval house at Llandough
x: The Neath Guardian of 17 April 1980 reported a talk by the assistant director of the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust on recent digs at Llandough, where substantial remains of a Roman villa and “part of a later medieval house” were found. The report did not locate the medieval house.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N05 — “Historical Society had notable year” (Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980)

t: 1949–51 county court books not yet searched
x: Cardiff County Court plaint and minute books for 1947–51 survive at Glamorgan Archives (ACA/2, ACA/3, ACA/6). The court that gave the arrears judgment against Frederick Buckler, paid off in 1953, is not stated by the Court of Appeal and its record has not been located. (source pending)

t: Great House rejected in 1988 listing survey
x: Cadw wrote in May 2026 that Great House Farm and the barn were “assessed and rejected for listing in the 1988 community survey of Llandough”, graded marginally below the bar on 29 July 1988. The list that survey produced was issued on 6 April 1989, listing three Llandough buildings.

t: c.1841: orchard, meadows and wood farmed
x: The c.1841 tithe apportionment for Landough, Cogan and Leckwith lists “Williams John” as occupier of 36 parcels, about 119½ acres, among them an orchard (no. 211, 1a 3r 19p), meadows and a wood (no. 219, 1a 3r 38p). The landowner listed for 33 of the parcels is the Marquess of Bute.
src: National Library of Wales tithe maps

t: 31 Jul 1972: VG41 objection period ends
x: The second objection period under the Commons Registration Act 1965 ends on 31 July 1972. It covers village green VG41, provisionally registered on 16 June 1970; notice of it was given by public notice only.

t: 1876–1912: 33 acres of the farm to limeworks
x: A National Library of Wales catalogue entry for the Bute deeds D153/4–8 lists “land (33 a.), formerly part of Great House Farm, for the Llandough Limeworks (33 a.), 1876-1912”, with a plan engrossed on D153/3 (1875) and D153/4 (1876). The deeds, their parties and the parcel have not yet been read.

t: 15 Dec 1887: obituary of Daniel Thomas
x: The obituary of Daniel Thomas of Penylan (Tarian y Gweithiwr, 15 December 1887) records him as a contractor under Lord Bute and owner of “valuable lime kilns at Llandough”. On 24 April 1888 a man is described as “a labourer at Llandough Quarry”.

t: 11 Aug 1889: “the property of John Williams”
x: Apples were taken from “the orchard of Great House Farm … the property of John Williams”, reached “over the hedge from the railway”. John Williams junior gave evidence (Barry Dock News, 16 August 1889).

t: 26 Nov 1896: J. E. Billups and the brickworks
x: The obituary of J. E. Billups (South Wales Daily News, 26 November 1896, p.6) records “the Penarth Brickworks, which were started by him”. A published brickworks history places the Llandough brickworks “next door” to the lime works “by 1899”, Billups Brick Co Ltd as proprietor, “Llandough Brick Co by 1923”, and “disused” by 1947 (secondary source).

t: 1 Apr 1907: air-rifle meeting at Great House Farm
x: The Llandough Air-rifle Club held its Easter Monday meeting “at Great House Farm, Llandough” (Evening Express, 27 March and 2 April 1907).

t: 6 Jan 1908: poacher caught on Great House Farm
x: A poacher was caught “poaching on Great House Farm, Llandough” by keepers on their round and given two months in gaol (Evening Express, 10 January 1908).

t: 17 Jul 1908: death of John Williams
x: The Baptist Record of October 1908 (Vol. 13 no. 139, p.27, Llandough notes) records “the death of Mr. John Williams, of Great House Farm, Llandough, which occurred on Friday, July 17th, and the burial on the 21st, aged 81”: a dated contemporary record of the 1908 death in Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement.

t: Oct 1910: John Williams on Bute’s Court Leet jury
x: At Bute’s Court Leet at Llandough, “John Williams” sat on the grand jury, which had “no presentments to make of the deaths of freeholders, or encroachments” (Barry Dock News, 14 October 1910; with the 1904–1917 reports).

t: 26 Mar 1925: damages for worried sheep
x: “Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough” brought a case for damages for sheep worried by dogs (Western Mail, 26 March 1925; snippet only).

t: 14 Dec 1927: death of Lord Pontypridd
x: Alfred Thomas, Lord Pontypridd, son of Daniel Thomas of the Llandough lime works, died unmarried. A report of 27 December 1927 records that “the bulk of his property” was left “unconditionally to the corporation” of Cardiff (source pending).

t: c. 1937–40: Mary’s eldest son born
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s eldest son was born in about 1937–40 (family record).

t: 6 Feb 1939: the farm still under the Williams name
x: A Western Mail notice read “LOST from Great House Farm, Twelve-bore Gun … —Williams, Llandough” (snippet only). The farm still advertised under the Williams name after the conveyance of 25 December 1938.

t: 17 Nov 1942: sale of farming stock advertised
x: The Western Mail advertised an “IMPORTANT SALE OF LIVE AND DEAD FARMING STOCK. GREAT HOUSE FARM, LLANDOUGH” (17 November 1942, p.2; snippet only). Which Llandough is meant is not yet confirmed.

t: 9 Oct 1957: Western Mail names Mrs M. D. Buckler
x: The Western Mail of 9 October 1957 (p.6) carries an item with the name “Mrs. M. D. BUCKLER … Llandough”. Only a search-result snippet is held; its content and subject have not yet been read.

t: 1968–69: eldest son’s household leaves the farm
x: Between September 1968 and September 1969 the household of Mary (Nancy) Williams’s eldest son left the farm (family record). A later recollection links this to a rumoured sale of a land parcel; no deed of any sale has been found.

t: 7 Feb 1981: BP Pension Trust sells ground rents
x: BP Pension Trust sold its residential freehold ground rents in South Wales to Cefn Estates (press snippets). Whether any of the farm land was in the sale is not shown.

t: 29 Jul 1983: BP Pension Trust house plan, Penlan Road
x: The South Wales Echo reported that Vale councillors would hold a site meeting in Llandough on “plans by the BP Pension Trust to build a house there … on land at Penlan Road”; the community council called the access “dangerous” (snippet). Whether the plot was farm land is not yet confirmed.

t: 6 May 1987: dispute on the Echo’s front page
x: The South Wales Echo reported the dispute on its front page on 6 May 1987, between the High Court judgment of July 1986 and the appeal.

t: Jan 1989: summons withdrawn as out of time
x: A threatening-behaviour summons over events of 29 April 1988 was withdrawn in January 1989 as out of time (press).

t: 8 Feb 1990: GGAT comments missing from file
x: Further comments from the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust dated 8 February 1990 (Appendix B to the planning report) are missing from the planning file.
src: Redevelopment and Church View Close (Legal Wiki)

t: Dec 1993: groundworks before the archaeology condition
x: Groundworks on the site began in December 1993, before the planning condition on archaeology had been met.

t: 14 Nov 2025: report sent to the local MP
x: The family wrote to the local MP with a report on the case; the Community Council clerk appears to have been copied (MPs correspondence M47).

t: 14 Nov 2025: one reply from a Vale councillor
x: A Vale of Glamorgan councillor replied once, “If you’d like to discuss, please let me know”, and did not answer six later emails (Vale correspondence M49).
src: Vale of Glamorgan Council correspondence (Legal Wiki)

t: 2 Feb 2026: HM Land Registry asks for details
x: HM Land Registry Customer Support asked for the title number and details of the suspected 1982 irregularities (HMLR correspondence M03).

t: 6 Feb 2026: emails passed to a senior officer
x: HM Land Registry referred the family’s emails on title WA231076 to a senior officer (HMLR correspondence M05).

t: 12–13 Mar 2026: FOI stalls without a title number
x: HM Land Registry’s FOI team replied that it could not proceed without a title number (HMLR correspondence M11, M14).

t: 18 May 2026: FOI request to the Community Council
x: The family asked Llandough Community Council for all its records on the farm under FOI, including any record of William (Billy) Buckler addressing the council around 1988 (LCC correspondence M04).

t: 14 Jun 2026: 1982 minutes sent to the archives
x: The Community Council clerk replied that minutes from 1982 were deposited at Glamorgan Archives in 2002 (section 21 FOIA). The family’s follow-up of the same day was still unanswered after 126 days, at 18 October 2026 (LCC correspondence M06, M07).

t: 13 Oct 2026: internal review asked of the Council
x: The family asked Llandough Community Council for an internal review; the clerk sent the agenda for 22 October at 7pm, with the public able to attend “in person or remotely” (LCC correspondence M18).

t: 16 Oct 2026: meeting moved to remote only
x: The Community Council clerk wrote that the 22 October meeting “will now be held remotely only”. The family objected the same day and had no reply by 18 October (LCC correspondence M22, M23).

t: 1904: John Williams, Bute tenant since 1855
x: The Cardiff Times of 16 July 1904 reported Mr John Williams “of Llandough Farm” as a guest at the Marquess of Bute’s rent audit dinner: “He succeeded his father in the tenancy of the farm in 1855 … Saturday was his 102nd rent audit.” The paper names Llandough Farm, not Great House.

t: High Court summons against BP, Dec 1988
x: The South Wales Echo of 2 December 1988 reported that a summons against BP would be heard on Monday 5 December; Mr Justice Anthony Evans allowed that the family could enter the house to collect belongings only “as long as BP solicitors agree”. The family had also lodged a petition.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-05 — South Wales Echo search extract, Friday 2 December 1988

t: NPCC: 1988 operation absent from ACPO listings
x: The National Police Chiefs’ Council answered FOI 3156/2026 on 16 September 2026: searches of ACPO archive listings available to it found no references to Great House Farm, Llandough, BP Properties Ltd v Buckler or the 1988 operation, and it held nothing on where such records went.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R49 — NPCC FOI 3156/2026 response (16 September 2026)

t: Cadw officers survey the house, 1988
x: Branwen, who lived at Great House Farm until 1988, stated that Cadw officers came into the house in 1988, carried out a survey and remarked on the roof beams being high. Cadw’s two inspection photographs are dated 29 July 1988; its decision not to list was reported on 6 Dec 1988.

t: Woodland transferred to Forest of Cardiff, 1994
x: On 10 November 1994 the woodland beside the farm was transferred to Forest of Cardiff under title WA735527, after a chain from Western Ground Rents through BP and Ideal Homes. The register shows land tinted blue (the 1975 farmhouse strand) and pink (the 1982 Bute–WGR strand).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E149 — 10 November 1994 transfer of the woodland to Forest of Cardiff (WA735527), with plan and consideration

t: Llandough villagers meet councillors in anger
x: The South Wales Echo of 9 December 1988 reported a bid to stop BP Properties profiting from the demolition “earlier this week” of “an 800-year-old farmhouse”, and that a group of Llandough villagers met local councillors to express their anger at the way BP had demolished it.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-09 — South Wales Echo search extract, Friday 9 December 1988

t: Tree planting and ownership acts on Parcel A
x: Trees were planted on Parcel A as an act of ownership, and the house and land were occupied by the family for generations. Occupation by John Williams is documented from at least 1891; which trees were planted, when and by whom is still to be documented (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E151 — Family tree planting and other acts of ownership on Parcel A (long occupation evidence)

t: Reader’s letter: “just like a wartime sight”
x: A reader’s letter in the South Wales Echo of 21 December 1988 responded to the Echo’s 6 December report “Bulldozed Before Breakfast”: “How awful for the unfortunate Buckler family”. It ran with a photograph of Branwen and the children near the remains of the farmhouse.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-12 — South Wales Echo search extract, Wednesday 21 December 1988 (reader’s letter)

t: 1972 permission for about 13 houses
x: In 1972 BP Pension Trust obtained outline permission 3/8996/3337 for about 13 houses on the farm land while Mary (Nancy) Williams occupied the house and disputed ownership. No archaeological condition was attached; the ownership certificate has not yet been obtained.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E134 — 1972 outline planning permission 3/8996/3337 (about 13 houses) and ownership certificate

t: First eviction attempt: a dozen police present
x: The South Wales Echo of 30 April 1988 reported that “a dozen police officers were on the farm as the bailiffs tried to evict the Buckler family”, and that Mr Buckler refused to leave Great House Farm for a medical check-up because he feared the bailiffs would return.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-02 — Saturday 30 April 1988: South Wales Echo (British Newspaper Archive extract)

t: Evicted farmer freed after guilty plea, March 1989
x: The South Wales Echo of 23 March 1989 reported, under the headline “Evicted farmer freed after pleading guilty”, that the farmer who lost his home at Great House Farm when it was demolished “at the end of last year” had admitted two matters (cut off in the extract).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-15 — South Wales Echo search extract, Thursday 23 March 1989

t: 1949 unwritten tenancy to Frederick Buckler
x: Frederick Buckler held an unwritten yearly agricultural tenancy from 2 February 1949, recited in later documents and concerning Parcel B; no written agreement exists. Mary refused a tenancy of the farmhouse at the same time and asserted ownership (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E122 — 2 February 1949 surrender and re-grant of Frederick Buckler’s tenancy (no written record)

t: 1989 planning report: appendices B–E missing
x: The 1989 officer’s report on application 89/01396/OUT dealt with the demolition in one clause, and its appendices B–E are missing. Outline permission was granted on 13 March 1990. A later planning document called the house “a listed building”, which it never was.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E146 — 1989 planning officer’s report 89/01396/OUT (appendices B–E missing) and the 13 March 1990 outline permission

t: Councillor and BP pensioner calls demolition “disgusting”
x: The South Wales Echo of 7 December 1988 (Peter Collins) reported that a Vale of Glamorgan councillor who was also a BP pensioner called BP Properties’ decision to flatten the buildings “disgusting” and planned to write in protest over the 33-year family battle.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-08 — South Wales Echo search extract, Wednesday 7 December 1988 (Peter Collins)

t: WGR sells Llandough land to developers, 1962
x: On 5 March 1962 Western Ground Rents conveyed land at Llandough “with other property” to Lakeside and Llandough Development Co Ltd, taking a £75,000 charge; on 11 June 1965 both conveyed a parcel to Glamorgan County Council (Vale FOI reply, 14 September 2026).

t: Bail conditions changed for evicted farmer
x: The South Wales Echo of 6 January 1989 reported, under “Bail change for evicted farmer”, that Mr Buckler, 40, had his bail conditions changed on charges of assault, criminal damage and wanton or furious driving, after the house was “demolished late last year”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-13 — South Wales Echo search extract, Friday 6 January 1989

t: 1938 conveyance offered as root of title
x: A 1965 contract for the sale of the Llandough school site set special condition F: “Title shall be deduced, and shall commence … with a Conveyance on sale dated 25th December 1938”, making the 1938 conveyance the root of title offered for this Llandough land.

t: Historical map labelled “1841-map”
x: A historical map labelled “1841-map”, likely linked to the tithe survey, is held. It can help reconstruct the field names and the boundaries of the Great House Farm parcels; its exact title and archive reference are still to be confirmed (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E165 — Historical map labelled “1841-map” (original image upload)

t: South Wales Police: no records held for 1988
x: South Wales Police answered FOI request 719/26 on 16 July 2026 with a “no records held” result for the 1988 events at Great House Farm. The answer covers only the search the force described; incident logs, orders and warrants from 1988 remain unlocated.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R38-A1 — South Wales Police FOI 719/26 response, 16 July 2026

t: Lodger placed at the farmhouse, June 1950
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c.1974 witness statement names a lodger placed at the farmhouse in June 1950 and records his conviction for theft c. 1951–52. The Penarth petty sessions registers that would confirm it have not yet been searched (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E124 — Penarth petty sessions record: the lodger (Bruce Sutherland), c. 1951–52

t: 1975 conveyance: BP Pension Trust to BP Properties
x: On 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust conveyed the farmhouse and garden to BP Properties, the first conveyance into the company that had issued the October 1974 licence. Title WA240304 was later registered on it; its plan (item 13) is dated 23 February 1975.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E138 — 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust to BP Properties conveyance and plan (WA240304 items 1, 12, 13)

t: HM Land Registry: “no evidence of a mistake”
x: HM Land Registry’s letter of 23 March 2026 on the registration history recorded the WA231076 application as received 30 November 1982 and WA240304 on 23 February 1983, the titles later amalgamated, and found “no evidence of a mistake in the register”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E156 — HM Land Registry letter about the registration history of Tŷ Mawr Farm, 23 March 2026

t: Open day to save Tŷ Mawr, 1974
x: The Daily Telegraph reported that on 15 April 1974 Mary (Nancy) Williams held a public open day at Ty Mawr against planned demolition: “The ownership of the house has been in dispute for 25 years but my family has lived here for more than 400 years.”

t: Community Council refuses records request on cost
x: On 11 October 2026 Llandough Community Council refused a request for post-2002 records, images of the farm, green and church, and 1982 transfer records under section 12 (cost limit), offering a narrower 2002–2006 period and internal review (EV-0177).

t: 1908 court leet honours John Williams, juror
x: The Barry Dock News of 23 Oct 1908 reported the court leet and court baron of the lordship of Bute at Llandough passing “a vote of sympathy … with the family of the late Mr. John Williams, Great House, Llandough, for many years a juror of the court.”

t: 1961 deed: WGR, brickworks company and Cardiff
x: A deed of 29 March 1961 between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City, recited on woodland title WA735527, affected land now in the woodland title. It is not a Buckler family sale; the land and plan are still to be mapped.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E129 — 29 March 1961 deed: WGR, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City

t: 1916 tenancy of “the whole of the farm”
x: In February 1916 the Marquis of Bute granted John Williams a yearly agricultural tenancy of “the whole of the farm”, known only as recited in the 1987 judgment. No plan has been produced to show whether it included the house parcel separated in 1877.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E118 — February 1916 Bute yearly tenancy to John Williams, with plan

t: Forced entry and roof stripped, 30 Nov 1988
x: The South Wales Echo of 30 November 1988 reported that those who “forced their way into the 400-year-old Great House Farm” already had “half the roof off one of the outbuildings”, and that Branwen feared BP Properties would now flatten the farmhouse.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-04 — South Wales Echo search extract, Wednesday 30 November 1988

t: Llandough Farm was a separate Rees holding
x: The Rees family held a farm called Llandough Farm, rented from the Bute estate, from at least 1865 to 1910. It is named separately from John Williams’s Great House farm, so records naming “Llandough Farm” do not by themselves refer to Great House.

t: Lorries clear the site, 20 March 1989
x: The South Wales Echo of 20 March 1989 reported that lorries moved onto the site at 7.30am for an operation “likely to take several days”, after something was brought “to the ground by BP Properties following a 30 year legal battle over ownership”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-14 — South Wales Echo search extract, Monday 20 March 1989

t: c.1841 tithe: Williams occupier of Bute parcels
x: The c.1841 tithe apportionment for Landough, Cogan and Leckwith lists John Williams as occupier of 36 parcels, about 119½ acres: 33 owned by “Bute the Marquess of” and 3 glebe parcels of the Revd James Evans. No lease, term or rent is recorded.

t: Mary’s “previous statement” of 1955–62 missing
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c.1974 statement refers to a “previous statement” she made on the 1955 and 1962 applications. It has not been found on any court file; if it records her assertion of ownership, the other side knew of it by 1955 or 1962.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E127 — Mary (Nancy) Williams’s “previous statement” on the 1955 and 1962 applications

t: Death of William (Billy) Buckler, 1990
x: The 1991 probate calendar records “BUCKLER, William Beverley of [Penarth] S Glam died 29 April 1990 Administration Llandaff 11 July”, a probable match for William (Billy) Buckler. Another record gives 29 May 1990; the conflict is unresolved.

t: Alun Michael MP asks Lord Chancellor to look
x: The South Wales Echo of 12 May 1988 reported that Cardiff MP Alun Michael had asked the Lord Chancellor to look at the case of farmer Bill Buckler, who had resisted the bailiffs, and printed Mr Buckler’s warning that someone could be killed.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-03 — Thursday 12 May 1988: South Wales Echo (British Newspaper Archive extract)

t: Hansard 1980: BP fund criticised as ground landlord
x: In the Commons on 22 May 1980 Ted Rowlands MP stated that Western Ground Rents had been bought by the BP pension fund and that the fund was behaving harshly towards householders as a ground landlord. The debate did not name Great House Farm.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N16 — House of Commons, 22 May 1980: Ted Rowlands MP on BP and Western Ground Rents (Hansard)

t: House of Lords leave-to-appeal petition, 1987
x: After the 1987 Court of Appeal decision, leave to appeal was sought from the House of Lords. The petition papers, identified at The National Archives in September 2026, contradict the 1988 public statement that Mr Buckler “did not appeal”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E142 — 1987 House of Lords petition for leave to appeal: papers

t: Farmer freed on bail after demolition week
x: The South Wales Echo of 10 December 1988 reported that Mr Buckler, 40, who lived with his family at Great House Farm until BP Properties demolished it that week, had been freed on bail by magistrates the day before, on charges he faced.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-10 — South Wales Echo search extract, Saturday 10 December 1988

t: Bute’s will leaves Leckwith-with-Llandough estates
x: Newspapers of 18–20 October 1900 reported that the 3rd Marquess of Bute’s will left “all his estates in the parishes of Leckwith, with Llandough” and neighbouring parishes to Lord Colum Crichton-Stuart. The will itself is not yet seen.

t: William Rees: Tŷ Mawr “the manorhouse of Llandough”
x: A Western Mail letter signed “William Rees, Penarth” opposed demolition of Great House Farm, describing the farmstead of Great House, or Ty Mawr, as “serving as the manorhouse of Llandough” (GHF-E090-N04; year of the cutting unclear).

t: Western Ground Rents wound up, 1996
x: The London Gazette of 3 July 1996 listed Western Ground Rents Ltd (no. 342092), the 1938 buyer of the Bute estate, among dormant BP group companies at BP House, Hemel Hempstead, with a liquidator appointed by members on 26 June 1996.

t: 1958 objection: “It’s a Crichel Down”
x: On 20 November 1958 the Western Mail reported Mrs M. D. Buckler objecting to further industrial development near her farm, Ty Mawr, Llandough, and stating that land farmed by her family since 1667 had been “wrongfully appropriated”.

t: Title plan for WA231076, Sept 2026
x: The current title plan for WA231076 maps the extent now registered to others over the farm land. It is the plan to compare with the 1982 first-registration application and its lodged plans, and with the Parcel A / Parcel B division.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E162 — WA231076 title plan, September 2026

t: 1971 abstract of title not on the file
x: Later instruments recite a 1971 abstract of title for BP Pension Trust, but it is not a free-standing item on the HM Land Registry file. It is the best single record of the root BP’s side relied on, and its whereabouts are unknown.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E132 — 1971 abstract of title (BP Pension Trust)

t: Welsh Government: records destroyed under retention schedule
x: Welsh Government’s ATISN 26-0010 response recorded: “No files were found and given the date range of your request, any routine records would have been destroyed in line with the corporate retention schedule applied at the time.”

t: Llandough archaeology and the Roman villa
x: The Glamorgan Village Book (Glamorgan Federation of Women’s Institutes) printed a page on Llandough’s historical and archaeological material, including the Roman villa and its excavation, the wider setting of Great House Farm.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E110-A7 — The Glamorgan Village Book: Llandough archaeology context

t: A different “Great House Farm” sold in 1938
x: In November 1938 a 185-acre Great House Farm at Llandough near Cowbridge was auctioned and reported sold to L. D. Thomas of Porthcawl for £5,500 (Western Mail). It is a different property from Tŷ Mawr, Llandough near Penarth.

t: Fire destroys Trust’s excavation finds, 1983
x: The South Wales Echo of 18 March 1983 reported that a fire at the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust’s Swansea warehouse destroyed excavation finds, including Llandough Roman villa material; about 90% was unrecoverable.

t: Churchview Close built on Great House Farm site
x: Press reports of 1994–96 recorded Ideal Homes (Wales) building “Churchview Close”, Llandough, and council payments to “contractors working on the nearby Great House Farm housing development” to regrass the village green.

t: Llandough manor return located at The National Archives
x: On 26 February 2026 The National Archives located the single return for the Manor of Llandough in the original returns to the Manorial Documents Committee (HMC 9/311), a lead to the manor’s records and their custodians.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R34-A1 — The National Archives Manorial Documents Register: HMC 9.311 Llandough manor return, 26 February 2026

t: GGAT 1992 warning letter: page 2 missing
x: The Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust wrote a warning letter on 27 July 1992; page 2 of it is missing from the record. Reserved matters (92/00671/RES) were approved 38 days later with no new archaeological condition.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E147 — 27 July 1992 GGAT letter (page 2 missing) and the reserved-matters approval 92/00671/RES

t: Police chiefs’ council: no information held
x: The National Police Chiefs’ Council’s FOI 3065/2026 response, searching “Great House Farm” and “Llandough”, listed the repositories and functions consulted and recorded no information held under questions 4, 5 and 6.

t: Bute “allowed her family a slice of land”
x: At the 6 May 1958 Leckwith Common inquiry Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler stated that about 130 years earlier Lord Bute had allowed her family “a slice of land”, a right of way and grazing rights (Western Mail, 7 May 1958).

t: Cadw declines 1988 listing request as repeat
x: Cadw / Welsh Government’s ATISN 27589 response to a request for July–December 1988 listing records declined it as “substantially similar” to an earlier request (ATISN 27021) already answered and internally reviewed.

t: Woodland registered under title WA735527
x: The September 2026 register for title WA735527 records the woodland next to the farm in other hands. It follows the 10 November 1994 transfer to Forest of Cardiff and the 2005 excision of land to Goldsworthy Homes.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E163 — WA735527 title register, September 2026

t: 1870s rate books: Williams occupier, Bute owner
x: Llandough poor-rate books of 1872–1876 list “John Williams | Lord Bute | Farm”: John Williams rated as occupier of a farm (about 76 acres) owned by Lord Bute, with Lord Bute rated for woods in his own occupation.

t: John Williams of Great House Farm, 1891
x: A magistrates’ court report of November 1891 named “Mr John Williams of Great House Farm, Llandough” as the owner of three geese taken on 11 November 1891, the earliest press record of John Williams at the farm.

t: Map of Tŷ Mawr dated 1824
x: An image titled “1824 map of Ty Mawr” is held. It shows Tŷ Mawr as a named holding in the early nineteenth century; its creator, series and scale are still to be confirmed from the original (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E166 — Map of Ty Mawr dated 1824 (image upload)

t: Title register for WA231076, Sept 2026
x: The September 2026 register for WA231076 is the present-day registration of the farm land. Its proprietorship entries and referred instruments stand on the first registration applied for on 30 November 1982.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E161 — WA231076 title register, September 2026

t: Cadw photograph of the barn, 29 July 1988
x: A Cadw survey photograph of the Great House Farm barn, dated 29 July 1988, was disclosed on 11 June 2026. It records the building’s appearance in the heritage-record trail four months before the demolition.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R37-A3 — Cadw barn survey photograph dated 29 July 1988, disclosed 11 June 2026

t: 2005 woodland sale to Goldsworthy Homes
x: On 2 December 2005 Forest of Cardiff transferred land out of woodland title WA735527 to Goldsworthy Homes Ltd. The charity’s accounts to 30 June 2006 record “Sale of Land — Leckwith Road, Llandough 20,000”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E150 — 2005 Forest of Cardiff to Goldsworthy Homes transfer and excision from WA735527

t: 1938: Leckwith Woods given to Cardiff council
x: A secondary source records that Western Ground Rents Ltd bought the Bute urban estate in 1938 and that Cardiff council acquired “some 109 acres” of Leckwith Woods “as a gift from Western Ground Rents Ltd”.

t: Cwm Cydfin wood notified as SSSI
x: Cwm Cydfin, Leckwith, “a mixed deciduous woodland adjacent to saltings of the River Ely” of 5.5 ha (ST 165739), was notified as a Site of Special Scientific Interest in 1972 and re-notified on 9 Dec 1985.

t: Cardiff leases Leckwith Woods for 999 years
x: The Western Mail of 18 March and 28 October 1955 reported that Cardiff held a 176-acre Leckwith Woods, “bought … for a nominal sum in 1942”, with 106 acres leased to the Forestry Commission for 999 years.

t: 1990: homes bid for Great House Farm land
x: The South Wales Echo of 23 Feb 1990 reported that “company chiefs are bidding [to] build homes on land where battling South Wales farmer Billy Buckler fought unsuccessfully to stop bailiffs evicting him”.

t: “All I’ve got left are the clothes”
x: The South Wales Echo of 13 December 1988 quoted Mr Buckler, evicted from Great House Farm by BP Properties, “who demolished the building a week later”: “All I’ve got left are the clothes [I] stand up in.”
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-11 — South Wales Echo search extract, Tuesday 13 December 1988

t: “I will fight on to the death”, 1989
x: The South Wales Echo of 24 March 1989 reported, under a “farmer freed” headline, that Billy Buckler vowed to continue his fight over the loss of his historic family home and “more than 70 acres of land”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-16 — South Wales Echo search extract, Friday 24 March 1989

t: 1877 Clyde Street lease is not the farm
x: A counterpart lease dated 6 Nov 1877 from the Bute Trustees to “Mr John Williams” is a 99-year building lease of a house plot in Clyde Street, Roath, granted to a builder. It is not a lease of the farm.

t: Tree planting and occupation across Parcel A
x: Tree planting and other acts of occupation on Parcel A, from 1891 to 1955 and after, are catalogued at EV-0009 and GHF-E151; a photograph of tree planting at the farm is held (EV-0199, date unknown).

t: “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”
x: The South Wales Echo front page of about 30 November 1988 (Peter Bibby) carried the headlines “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”, “A bitter feud over rights that lasted 33 years” and “Action on farm”.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N14 — “Angry scenes as farmer evicted” (South Wales Echo front page, c. 30 November 1988)

t: Farmer taken from hospital bed to face charges
x: The South Wales Echo of 3 December 1988 reported that evicted farmer Bill Buckler, 40, “caught up in a 33-year wrangle”, was taken from his hospital bed to face charges of assaulting two bailiffs.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15-06 — South Wales Echo search extract, Saturday 3 December 1988

t: John Williams of Great House Farm, 1891
x: A November 1891 newspaper reported that Robert Williams was charged with stealing three geese from Mr John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough, on 11 November 1891, and was remanded to Penarth.

t: “BP signal Welsh sales”, July 1988
x: On 9 July 1988, between the April stand-off and the November eviction, the Estates Gazette reported “BP signal Welsh sales”, naming Ropemaker Properties with Debenham Tewson as agents (EV-0093).

t: 1902 Bute auction of Cwm Cydfin Wood
x: Glamorgan Archives file DSA/3/192 records the Marquess of Bute selling coppice woods at auction on 29 Nov 1902, including “Cwm Cydfin Wood (Leckwith and Llandough)” and part of Coed-y-Ddylluan.

t: HM Land Registry final complaint decision
x: HM Land Registry’s stage-two decision of 25 May 2026, its “second and final response”, held that the title is registered correctly. The decision went on to the Independent Complaints Reviewer.

t: Bute conveyance of 23 February 1905
x: A Bute conveyance of 23 February 1905, a deed with Cardiff Corporation, is referred to on the WA231076 first-registration file and burdens part of the later woodland title (EV; not yet held).

t: Archive note: Nancy, daughter of John Williams
x: Glamorgan Archives D/D XJF 64/30–31 holds a note identifying Nancy Buckler of Great House Farm as the daughter of John Williams of Great House Farm (born c. 1867), with her sketch (EV-0155).

t: 1936 wedding: Fred Buckler and Mary (Nancy) Williams
x: The Western Mail of 5 Aug 1936 reported, under “LLANDOUGH BRIDE”, the wedding at Llandough Church of Fred Buckler, of Barry, and Mary Doreen (Nancy) Williams, of Great House Farm, Llandough.

t: Photograph of tree planting at Great House Farm
x: A photograph titled “tree planting at Great House Farm” is held in the evidence library (item EV-0199). The date, photographer and exact scene have not been established (source pending).

t: Community council refuses minutes search on cost
x: Llandough Community Council refused the 21 September 2026 information request under FOIA section 12, citing the cost limit for searching council and committee minutes. (source pending)

t: Diary lists three Daniel Thomas receipts, 1903–10
x: William Buckler’s 1983 diary records three receipts associated with Daniel Thomas, dated 30 June 1903, 31 December 1906 and 31 March 1910. The receipts themselves are not held.

t: First-registration application, 23 Feb 1983
x: HM Land Registry file WA240304 item 10 is the register and first-registration application of 23 February 1983, made a month before Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983.

t: County court registers: arrears, possession, committal
x: Cardiff County Court registers at Glamorgan Archives (ACA, 1953–1975) are catalogued as covering the 1953 arrears action, the 1962 possession order and a 1963 committal.

t: Title plan for WA513690, Sept 2026
x: The current title plan for WA513690 shows another registered extent over land linked to the farm, part of the chain of titles WA231076, WA240304, WA513690 and WA735527.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E160 — WA513690 title plan, September 2026

t: County Council acquires land near Cogan Pill, 1958
x: A Western Mail legal notice of 24 September 1958 recorded a Glamorgan County Council acquisition of land near Cogan Pill, listing Western Ground Rents as owner.

t: 1864: Amy Williams, widow of Great House, dies
x: Death notices of 30 Dec 1864 recorded that Amy Williams, widow of John Williams of Great House farm, Llandough, died at Llandough on 23 Dec 1864, aged 65.

t: HM Land Registry FOI F260213: bundle disclosure refused
x: HM Land Registry answered FOI request F260213 on 13 April 2026, confirming the registration and refusing disclosure of the registration bundle under FOI.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R35-A1 — HM Land Registry FOI F260213 response, 13 April 2026

t: HM Land Registry stage-one complaint decision
x: HM Land Registry issued its stage-one complaint decision on the registration of the farm on 19 April 2026. A stage-two complaint was lodged the same day.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E154 — HM Land Registry stage-one complaint decision, 19 April 2026

t: Vale councillors authorise action against BP, 1989
x: On 11 February 1989 the South Wales Echo reported that Vale councillors had authorised legal action against BP Properties over the demolition (EV-0117).

t: Forest of Cardiff sells Leckwith Road land
x: Forest of Cardiff’s accounts to 30 June 2006, note 13, record “Sale of Land — Leckwith Road, Llandough 20,000” as other income, nil in the year before.

t: 1894: Williams pig herd at Great House
x: Barry Dock News reported swine fever at Llandough in 1894: Mr Williams of Great House kept a herd of over 20 pigs and at least five were slaughtered.

t: 1891: geese stolen from Great House Farm
x: The South Wales Star of 10 June 1892 reported geese stolen, “the property of Mr. John Williams, Great House Farm, Llandough, on November 11, 1891”.

t: Llandough Manor in the Manorial Documents Register
x: The National Archives’ Manorial Documents Register holds a Llandough Manor return (HMC 9.311), a catalogue lead for the manor’s records (EV-0146).

t: Wales Office FOI 26FOI 103 referred elsewhere
x: The Wales Office answered FOI request 26FOI 103 on 22 September 2026 and pointed to the Welsh Government rather than supplying records itself.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R16-A1 — Wales Office response to FOI 26FOI 103, 22 September 2026

t: Reserved-matters application for 20 houses, 1992
x: On 14 May 1992 an application for approval of reserved matters was made for 20 detached houses at Great House Farm, Leckwith Road (EV-0127).

t: Farm noted in conservation reports, 1983
x: The South Wales Echo of 26 October 1983 reported Great House Farm noted in conservation reports by the Community Council and Vale planners.

t: Monuments record: “building destroyed by owners”
x: The Sites and Monuments Record card PRN 02038s, dated March 1989, records the farmhouse as “building destroyed by owners” (EV-0118).

t: Woodland transferred to Forest of Cardiff, 1994
x: On 10 November 1994 the woodland was transferred to the Forest of Cardiff, title WA735527, with plan (EV-0136; deed not yet held).

t: Mary’s “previous statement” missing
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s “previous statement” on the 1955 and 1962 applications, referred to in the record, is missing (GHF-E127).

t: Map of Tŷ Mawr dated 1824
x: A map of Ty Mawr dated 1824 is held (EV-0004); whether 1824 is the map date or an associated reference is not yet established.

t: Press: “800 year-old farm house” razed
x: A press cutting of about 7 December 1988 was headlined “Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last” (EV-0106).

t: Title register for WA513690, Sept 2026
x: The September 2026 register for title WA513690 records a further registered title over land linked to Great House Farm.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E159 — WA513690 title register, September 2026

t: Frederick’s tenancy surrendered and re-granted, 1949
x: On 2 February 1949 Frederick Buckler’s yearly tenancy was surrendered and re-granted. No written record of it exists.

t: Local Plan: buildings on site to be retained
x: The East Vale Local Plan of February 1987 stated that the buildings on the Great House Farm site were to be retained.

t: Cwm-Cedwyn: wooded dell on the Ely
x: Cwm-Cedwyn is recorded as the name of a wooded dell on the River Ely between Leckwith and Llandough. (source pending)

t: Part of woodland transferred to Goldsworthy Homes, 2005
x: In 2005 the Forest of Cardiff transferred land excised from woodland title WA735527 to Goldsworthy Homes (EV-0139).

t: Herbert grants Vaughan 1,000-year lease of Cydwin
x: In 1547 Sir George Herbert granted Vaughan a 1,000-year lease of Cydwin (EV-0002; primary document not yet held).

t: 1959: child hurt near Great House Farm home
x: The Western Mail of 27 Nov 1959 reported a five-year-old girl hurt near her home at Great House Farm, Llandough.

t: Historical map labelled “1841-map”
x: A historical map labelled “1841-map” is held (EV-0005); its survey or edition date is not yet established.

t: Directories place John Williams at Great House
x: Trade directories of 1868, 1875, 1880, 1887, 1891 and 1901 list John Williams at “Great House”, Llandough.

t: Published Llandough history names Great House Farm
x: A printed local history page headed “Llandough (Penarth)” refers to Great House Farm. (source pending)

t: Cwm-Cedwyn in Llandough boundary records, 1392
x: Llandough boundary records of 1392 refer to Cwm-Cedwyn (EV-0001; primary document not yet held).

t: 1987: BP “registered proprietors” since 1982
x: The 1987 appeal was “limited to the farmhouse itself and its garden”. The court recited that BP “have the paper title to the farm, and indeed since November 1982 they have been the registered proprietors”, found Frederick and Mary in adverse possession from February 1955, but held title not extinguished because of the 1962 order and 1974 licence.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Four-hour stand-off with bailiffs, 29 Apr 1988
x: Five bailiffs and about 15 police arrived. William Buckler blocked the drive with a tractor and barred the doors; bailiffs broke the doors with poleaxes and withdrew after a four-hour stand-off. William told the press: “They have got no documents for it. If it’s theirs, why have I never paid a penny in rent for it in my life?” (N07)

t: Mary’s statement: freehold to pass when quarrying ceased
x: In her c.1974 statement Mary (Nancy) Williams described an 1877 division: the Bute Estate served notice to quit, sold “the farmhouse and buildings and about 10 acres” to Daniel Thomas and kept “about 9 acres up on the top”; her grandfather rented from both, rent fell as quarrying took land, and the freehold would then pass to him.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

t: 4 July 1955: forest and green taken
x: On 4 July 1955, enforcing possession under wording describing the “whole farm”, Western Ground Rents took the forest north of the house and the south-eastern ground later registered as village green VG41. Mary, after a recent leg amputation and with seven children, held the farmhouse, buildings and garden. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: Demolition begins within hours of eviction
x: The South Wales Echo of 3 December 1988 reported that demolition began within hours of the bailiffs forcing entry, although a High Court judge had issued an interim injunction that the farmhouse and contents must not be touched. William Buckler, in hospital since the eviction, was taken to face assault charges (N08, N15).

t: WGR document reads as a small grazing let
x: The typed terms of a WGR document signed by John Williams show a monthly let at 8s, kept “as meadow or pasture”, filed by the DBDT catalogue among small Llandough plot lets. It reads as a separate grazing let, not a revised farm tenancy; page 1 (parcels and acreage) is not online (EV-0023). Compare the 1939 plan square.

t: “Whole farm” wording merges Parcels A and B
x: Working theory: the 1955 “whole farm” wording merged Parcel A with Frederick Buckler’s Parcel B agricultural tenancy, and enforcement took the north forest and south-east green along with Parcel B. Mary defended the house, buildings and garden but could not hold the whole Parcel A perimeter (source pending: EV-0032).
src: Legal Wiki: 1955 Parcel-A Loss Dossier — Woodland + VG41 Green

t: “Have walked in and taken” the land, 1958
x: Western Mail, 20 Nov 1958, p.7, reported Mrs M. D. Buckler (Mary (Nancy) Williams) of Ty Mawr telling the county planning committee that three councils and Western Ground Rents “have walked in and taken” the land, let sites “over her head”, cut off her water for nearly 10 years, and that she lost her Friesian herd.
src: Legal Wiki: Press and Archive Leads — October 2026

t: Appeal court finds joint adverse possession from 1955
x: Dillon LJ described the trial judge’s treatment of Mary’s intention as paradoxical and found that Frederick and Mary were jointly in adverse possession of the farmhouse and garden from 2 February 1955. The appeal was dismissed because the 1962 order remained enforceable and the 1974 letters made Mary a licensee.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Injunction to stop demolition refused, 5 Dec 1988
x: On 5 December 1988 in Cardiff, Judge Norman Francis dismissed the Bucklers’ application for an injunction to stop BP damaging the building until the European Commission of Human Rights had considered the case. Cadw stated the house was not of sufficient architectural merit (Western Mail, 6 December 1988; N10).

t: A chain of “whole farm” descriptions
x: Working theory: each adverse step relies on the one before describing the land as “the farm” or “the whole farm”: the 1916 tenancy, the 1955 and 1962 orders, the 1969 and 1975 conveyances, the 1982–83 registration, the 1987 judgment. No independent conveyance of the house parcel into that chain has been seen.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Medieval ironwork under the rear wing, c.1880
x: The 1990 archaeological assessment of Great House Farm and Holbrook & Thomas, Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005), recorded medieval ironwork discovered under the house’s rear wing about 1880 and held by the National Museum of Wales. The Museum’s own records place its Llandough ironwork at Church Farm about 1858.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33 — Amgueddfa Cymru reply to FOI 2026-036 (5 & 7 October 2026): further collections search

t: MOD: no information found; Special Forces NCND
x: In its 10 October 2026 internal review of FOI2026/09190 the Ministry of Defence reported no matching information in archive, Army Secretariat and counter-terrorism searches, applied section 23(5) to neither confirm nor deny Special Forces-related information, and acknowledged a timeliness failure (GHF-E169).

t: c.1870: soldier in armour found under dining room
x: Two Royal Commission archive records describe a find under the farmhouse dining-room floor “in about 1870” of “the remains of a soldier in armour, his horse, a lance and shield”; one records that the house “was reputed to be the stable of a Castle” (Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974; Coflein 6048942, 6048944).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R01 — Royal Commission (RCAHMW) reply RC26-0375, 29 September 2026

t: Medieval spearhead and spur found at Llandough, c.1858
x: A letter headed Cogan Pill, 22 Nov 1931 (museum file 63.24), records that a spearhead, possibly 15th-century, and a rowel spur “was found a[t] Llandough Church Farm when digging foundations for some new buildings about 1858”, with about six skeletons. Whether Church Farm is Great House Farm is unresolved.

t: Matter framed as a “private legal matter”
x: The National Archives (23 Sep 2026) framed the matter as a “local land ownership dispute” with “no records to transfer” save the court case; the Vale council (2 Jun 2026) wrote that “it appears this was a private legal matter”. Public bodies registered, assessed for listing, planned and policed the site.

t: Working theory: 1877 arrangement took effect 1928
x: Working theory: the 1877 arrangement took effect in 1928 and passed the whole of Parcel A to the Williams: the farmhouse and buildings, yard, garden, the forest north of the house and the south-eastern ground later registered as village green VG41. Parcel B was the separate eastern agricultural fields.

t: Working theory: limitation ran out around 1940
x: Working theory: if possession of Parcel A became adverse around 1928, the twelve-year period under section 1 of the Real Property Limitation Act 1874 could have barred the former owner’s right of action by about 1940; if it began only in 1940, about 1952. Rent-free occupation alone does not prove this.

t: Last rent paid to Alfred Thomas, 1928
x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams records that the last quarry machinery left in 1928 and John Williams paid the last rent, about £4 a year, to Alfred Thomas: “I saw the receipt for this last payment of rent. After this my father regarded the farm as his own.” Rent continued on the fields only.

t: HTV report: “SAS style” eviction, “prime development land”
x: An HTV Wales report (GHF-E113), reporter Miles Fletcher, presenter Nicola Heywood-Thomas, described the eviction as “SAS style”, called the site “prime development land overlooking Cardiff”, and reported a High Court injunction stopping BP demolishing the farm. t: “It was the family history”: demolition, Dec 1988

t: Takhar: fraudulent judgment can be set aside
x: Takhar v Gracefield Developments Ltd [2019] UKSC 13 holds that a judgment obtained by fraud may be set aside by a fresh action without showing the fraud could not have been discovered earlier; the fraud must be material, an operative cause of the decision (RBS v Highland [2013] EWCA Civ 328).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review Addendum — 6 October 2026 Fresh Reassessment

t: Commission: loss justified by BP’s “rights as owner”
x: The Commission’s 14 April 1989 decision held the loss of the home lawful and justified to protect BP’s rights as owner, and found William had no “possession” in law because the courts held the property belonged to another. It ruled on the domestic findings without seeing the title documents.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: HTV “Eviction News Material”, 30 Nov 1988
x: National Library of Wales catalogue item 507738, “Eviction News Material, 30 November 1988”, records a one-minute HTV Wales item: bailiffs removing furniture, removal vans, and Branwen leaving the farm, with a report that the High Court granted an injunction stopping BP demolishing the farm.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

t: William Buckler applies to Strasbourg, 1988
x: On 3 May 1988 William Buckler applied to the European Commission of Human Rights (No. 14464/88), complaining of unfair trial and bias, interference with his home and possessions, and lack of an effective remedy. While it was pending BP took possession and demolished the farmhouse (EV-0122).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: 1939 tenancy plan and the 1955 limitation clock
x: The 1987 court started the limitation clock in February 1955, treating the farmhouse as within Frederick’s tenancy. Working theory: if the May 1939 tenancy plan of Western Ground Rents excludes the house, adverse possession ran from 1938–39 and completed about 1951, before the 1955 order.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: Woodland transferred to Forest of Cardiff, 1994
x: A transfer of 10 November 1994 put the woodland on title WA735527, combining land tinted blue (from the 1975 farmhouse conveyance) and pink (from the 1982 conveyance). Whether value was paid is open; a volunteer lacks a purchaser’s protection (Limitation Act 1980 s.32(3); LRA 2002 s.29).
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: 1988 heritage note released only in 2026
x: The full Historic Environment Record source file, including R. F. Suggett’s December 1988 note on the house, was in Heneb’s custody but was digitised and published only in October 2026, after an EIR request of 8 September 2026; the first substantive reply of 6 October did not supply it.

t: Quarrying and rent to Thomas end, 1928
x: Quarrying and rent payments to Alfred Thomas ended in 1928; the last rent receipt is catalogued as GHF-E120. Working theory: the 1877 arrangement then took effect, vesting the full Parcel A (farmhouse, buildings, yard, garden, north woodland) in the Williams family. Not a court finding.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E120 — 1928 last house-parcel rent receipt and end of quarrying (Thomas records)

t: Museum: no record of finds from the farm
x: Amgueddfa Cymru reported that its 1875–1915 predecessor registers hold no accession, register, day-book, donations-book or correspondence entry for finds from Great House Farm, Tŷ Mawr or Llandough Farm, and no record of ironwork associated with the farmhouse floor, rear wing or dairy.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33 — Amgueddfa Cymru reply to FOI 2026-036 (5 & 7 October 2026): further collections search

t: Limitation Act s.32: concealment postpones time
x: Section 32 of the Limitation Act 1980 postpones time where an action is based on fraud or a relevant fact was deliberately concealed; concealment needs no pre-existing duty to disclose (Canada Square v Potter [2023] UKSC 41). Section 32(3) protects a later innocent purchaser for value.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: 1877 promise gave at most an equitable right
x: A promise that the freehold “should belong to my grandfather” when quarrying ceased gave at most a contractual or equitable right; a deed was needed to pass the legal estate (Real Property Act 1845), and an open-ended promise may have been void against later owners (LSWR v Gomm, 1882).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Planning permission for 13 houses, 1972
x: In 1972 BP Pension Trust obtained planning permission for about 13 houses (3/8996/3337) while Mary occupied the house and disputed ownership. Applications then needed an ownership certificate naming every owner (Town and Country Planning Act 1962 s.16); the 1972 certificate is unseen.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1938 particulars: possibly a different farm
x: Sale particulars of 15 Nov 1938 (Glamorgan Archives DSA/6/1158) for “Great House Farm, Llandough” name D.J. Jenkins as owner and a sale for £5,500 to L.D. Thomas of Porthcawl. Possibly a different farm: a 1938 Western Mail report places a Great House Farm of that sale near Cowbridge.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree
Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R52 — Glamorgan Archives email, 11 June 2026

t: Record losses clustered around proceedings
x: Working theory: losses cluster around proceedings — family papers c.1950–52 before the 1955 action, the library copy of the Bute–Thomas deed in 1984 (the year of the writ), and RCAHMW’s Johns–Buckler correspondence “since 1986/87” (trial and appeal). Timing only; no causal finding.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: No Cadw record of 5 Dec 1988 decision
x: The only located source for a Cadw statement on 5 Dec 1988, the day before demolition, is the Western Mail of 6 Dec 1988. Cadw holds only two photographs of 29 July 1988, records no December inspectors’ visit, and declined to “speculate on the events around the listing assessment”.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Armour found under the dining-room floor
x: RCAHMW records (NMR 6048942; Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, NMR 6048944) place an armour find under the farmhouse dining-room floor about 1870; GGAT’s 1990 assessment places it under the rear wing c.1880. HER GGAT02038s records medieval ironwork and pottery reported from the site.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams, c.1974
x: Her witness statement (c.1974) reads: “My family have lived and farmed at Great House Farm since 1667.” “It was also provided that when the quarrying ceased the freehold should belong to my grandfather.” “I have never … paid rent to or acknowledged the title of anyone as landlord.”
src: Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

t: 1952 letter: WGR would not proceed with letting
x: The published 1987 Court of Appeal report records a 10 October 1952 agents’ letter stating that Western Ground Rents did not propose to proceed with the letting, yet Dillon LJ concluded that Frederick had a protected periodic agricultural tenancy. The report does not mention 1954.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler
Legal Wiki: GHF-E182 — 1954 further attempt to treat Frederick Buckler as a tenant (source pending)

t: 1987 defence knew of the separate 1975 conveyance
x: In 1987 William’s side argued, as its “third argument”, that the farmhouse came under its own May 1975 conveyance. The lawyers therefore knew of the separate conveyance during the litigation, which weakens a later argument that the 1983 registration could not have been discovered.

t: Res judicata and abuse of process bar
x: A judgment binds the parties and their successors in title, including Mary's estate; points that could have been raised may be barred (Henderson v Henderson; Johnson v Gore Wood [2002] 2 AC 1), save for special circumstances such as new material (Arnold v NatWest [1991] 2 AC 93).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Bute will leaves Leckwith-with-Llandough to Lord Colum
x: The 3rd Marquess of Bute’s will of 30 July 1894, reported in October 1900, named Leckwith-with-Llandough, Michaelston-le-Pit, Cogan, Sully, Lavernock, Penarth and St Andrews among the estates for Lord Colum Crichton-Stuart. The original will is not yet inspected (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Press and Archive Leads — October 2026

t: Museum withholds farm finds as “not in scope”
x: On 25 Aug 2026 Museum Wales refused FOI 2026-024 as “not held”, while the same letter recorded that its searches found records of other archaeological discoveries at Great House Farm and Church Farm, withheld as “not in scope”. The Church Farm records were released on 5 Oct 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)

Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33-A3 — Museum Wales collections record 63.24/2: medieval iron spearhead, Llandough Church Farm, c. 1858

t: High Court judgment for BP, 24 Jul 1986
x: Mr Justice Hollis heard the case on 10 July 1986 and gave judgment on 24 July 1986. He held that the 1974 letters gave Mary a valid licence, so she was not in adverse possession. Judgment was for BP, the possession order suspended for six months (South Wales Echo, 25 July 1986).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: War Agricultural Committee pressure; Frederick manages farm
x: Mary's statement records: “During the war my father had difficulty in farming the land to the satisfaction of the War Agricultural Executive Committee, owing to his age and in 1944 it was arranged that my husband should give up his job and run the farm as Manager for my father.”

t: Homeowners protected from rectification
x: Under the Land Registration Act 2002, Schedule 4, the register cannot be rectified against a proprietor in possession without consent, save for fraud, lack of care or injustice. This protects the homeowners; land still registered to Persimmon and the woodland stand differently.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Mary's statement: 1877 Bute–Thomas arrangement
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams's c.1974 statement records an 1877 arrangement in which Bute sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas for quarrying, with the freehold to pass to the Williams family when quarrying ceased. The original deed and plan remain missing.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

t: LRA 2002: register alteration and rectification
x: The Land Registration Act 2002 provides alteration and rectification routes (Schedule 4) and an indemnity regime (Schedule 8). For the woodland, the remedy can be rectification if an identified polygon is family land, subject to protections for the later registered proprietor.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review Addendum — 6 October 2026 Fresh Reassessment

t: Statement: freehold to pass when quarrying ceased
x: Mary's statement: “the agreement provided that the rent should progressively decrease as land was taken for quarrying. It was also provided that when the quarrying ceased the freehold should belong to my grandfather.” The agreement was kept in the blanket box at the farmhouse.

t: Listing files: each body points to another
x: Cadw: 1980s records transferred to RCAHMW or destroyed under the Public Records Act 1958. RCAHMW: no letters or records on the site in its registered files. Wales Office: files went to the National Assembly (1999) and Welsh Government (2007). Welsh Government (Cadw): not held.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree
