t: First registration to BP while Mary lived there
x: HM Land Registry’s first registration placed Great House Farm land in BP’s registered ownership in 1982–83 while the occupier still lived at the farmhouse. Notice of the registration was first seen after Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, during the mourning period.
src: Legal Wiki: 1982–83 Registration & Opportunity to Object

t: Titles amalgamated while appeal was open, 1987
x: HM Land Registry’s history records two titles: WA231076 (applied for 30 Nov 1982) and WA240304 (23 Feb 1983, the farmhouse-and-garden title), both live at the judgment of 24 July 1986. Amalgamation was applied for on 2 Feb 1987, while the appeal was open, and WA240304 closed.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree
Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: Eviction tape catalogued “Not viewed”
x: The National Library of Wales record for the 30 November 1988 eviction tape reads “Not viewed”; the clip's position on the tape is unknown and no catalogue or online-publication date appears. The separate 5 December 1988 “Wales at Six” demolition report has not been located.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

t: Medieval timber building beside St Dochdwy's
x: Heneb record GGAT03583s records postholes of a possible medieval timber building immediately north of St Dochdwy's, in the Great House Farm excavation area, with 12th–14th-century pottery; the excavators describe a rectangular building of possible 13th- or 14th-century date.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

t: 1949 yearly tenancy granted to Frederick
x: An unwritten yearly agricultural tenancy to Frederick Buckler began on 2 Feb 1949. The Court of Appeal later held that he had a periodic agricultural tenancy protected by the Agricultural Holdings Act; the last rent is recorded as paid in 1953. Its parcel scope is disputed.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: Working theory: a synthetic Parcel A registered
x: Working theory: the 1982–83 registrations WA231076 and WA240304 created a registered plot that mimicked the historic Parcel A centre, without an independent root of title, and it was later combined with Parcel B. The original applications, deeds and plans would decide this.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr): The Williams–Buckler Dispute

t: Water cut off by order of WGR
x: From about 1948–49 the water supply to the farmhouse and grounds was cut off, inferred from the 1958 statement of Mary (Nancy) Buckler née Williams that it had been cut off “for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents”. Branwen recalled cattle drowning in the River Ely trying to reach water.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Village green VG41 registered, 1970
x: Village green VG41 was provisionally registered on 16 June 1970 under the Commons Registration Act 1965, whose registers had an ownership section; unclaimed land could be vested in the local authority (s.8). Who asserted ownership, and on what evidence, is not yet shown (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: Abrupt cut after “prime development land” line
x: The surviving clip cuts abruptly after the voice-over describes the land as “prime development land overlooking Cardiff” and shows a figure in paramilitary-style dress. Whether this was the original edit or a later re-edit is not established; no censorship finding is made.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

t: 1969 root of title missing from both files
x: Both BP conveyances recite a 31 December 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust as their root of title; it is not on either file's schedule. The 1987 judgment records the 23 May 1975 conveyance as “the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden”.
src: Legal Wiki: Western Ground Rents Ltd
Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd and BP Pension Trust

t: 1877 arrangement: freehold when quarrying ceased
x: Working theory: the 1877 Bute–Thomas arrangement made the end of quarrying and rent in 1928 the trigger for the Williams family to take the freehold of the Parcel A house and quarrying land, distinct from Parcel B, retained by Bute. The original instrument is unavailable.

t: “Whole farm” description conflated Parcels A and B
x: Working theory: the 1986–87 limitation and licence findings were applied to a conflated “whole farm” description that masked the distinction between Parcel A and Parcel B and the 1955 seizure of the Parcel A forest and green. Mary asserted ownership before the 1984 writ.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: ECHR application declared inadmissible, 1989
x: William Buckler applied to the European Commission of Human Rights on 3 May 1988 (No. 14464/88). BP took possession and demolished the house while it was pending. On 14 April 1989 the Commission declared it inadmissible, finding the loss of the home lawful and justified.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: First bailiff eviction attempt, 29 Apr 1988
x: A press report recorded five bailiffs and around 15 police officers at the first eviction attempt on 29 April 1988, with South Wales Police stating officers were there to prevent a breach of the peace. The South Wales Echo of 30 April reported a dozen police on the farm.
src: Legal Wiki: South Wales Police — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

t: Early-medieval monastic cemetery: over 1,000 burials
x: The 1994 excavations at Llandough uncovered an early-medieval monastic cemetery: 858 inhumations and 152 disarticulated groups in the preliminary count (Cotswold Archaeological Trust Report 94213), and 1,026 burials in the 2005 published total (Medieval Archaeology 49).

t: Woodland title built from two strands
x: Woodland title WA735527 contains land tinted blue, from the 1975 farmhouse conveyance, and land tinted pink, from a 1982 conveyance subject to Bute’s 1905 deed with Cardiff Corporation and Western Ground Rents’ 1961 deed. Only the blue part follows the farmhouse strand.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1962 county court jurisdiction limit
x: County court jurisdiction in December 1962 was limited to property of £100 net annual rateable value, rising to £400 only in 1963. Working theory: if the farmhouse exceeded £100, the order was made without jurisdiction; the 1956 and 1963 valuation lists would test this.

t: 1916: Bute let “the whole of the farm”
x: The 1987 judgment recites that in 1916 the Marquis of Bute let “the whole of the farm” to John Williams, and later correspondence accepts that the 1916 tenancy “embraced both areas”. Either Bute still owned the farmhouse in 1916, or “whole farm” meant only Bute’s part.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Working theory: “synthetic parcels” overlaid older interests
x: Working theory: a repeated sequence of broad estate descriptions, permissive-occupation framing, possession of defined areas, selective conveyances and registration made distinct historic parcels appear as one holding, or let parts disappear into separate title chains.
src: Legal Wiki: Cedwyn Estate Working Theory — Repeated Parcel Capture, Parcel A and the Llandough–Leckwith Land Question

t: 1990 archaeological assessment of Great House Farm
x: In August 1990 the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust wrote “Land at Great House Farm, Llandough: An Archaeological Assessment”, recording that it discussed redevelopment with Debenham Tewson after the December 1988 demolition and advised the Vale planning authority.
src: Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E029-01 — 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment: Great House Farm, Llandough
Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: Estoppel and abuse-of-process barrier to title
x: Title was not argued in 1984–87, so any title case now meets Henderson v Henderson abuse-of-process and issue-estoppel arguments; the exception is new material that could not have been found with reasonable diligence (Arnold v National Westminster Bank [1991] 2 AC 93).
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: Farm papers taken from the blanket box, 1950
x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams records that a lodger placed at the farmhouse in June 1950 by a Penarth estate agent later told her he had taken “the papers which were in the blanket box including the agreement relating to the farm” and given them to the agent.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Vaughan phase, Bute works and medieval pottery
x: GGAT linked the seventeenth-century phase of the house to the Vaughan family and nineteenth-century work to the Bute Estate. Features were recorded in situ in 1974, others in the rubble, and twelfth- to fourteenth-century pottery sherds were recovered by E. J. Beare.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: Working theory: woodland recoverable by rectification
x: Working theory: if an exact woodland polygon is shown to belong to the superior historic Williams title, and its later registration or transfer was a mistake or ineffective against that title, it can be recovered by rectification and restoration rather than purchase.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: 1986 trial lost; 1987 appeal dismissed
x: In 1986 Hollis J in the High Court rejected the adverse-possession defence, finding Frederick lacked the intention to possess. In 1987 the Court of Appeal (Dillon LJ) disagreed on intention but dismissed the appeal on the basis of the 1962 order and the 1974 letters.
src: Legal Wiki: High Court — Forensic Assessment

t: Absolute title may rest on unsupported extent
x: Working theory: if HM Land Registry accepted absolute title to land whose extent the applicant’s deeds and prior title did not support, that would raise a question of registration mistake. The application plan, deeds, abstract and examination record would settle it.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

t: Was the Parcel B plan withheld?
x: Working theory: the landlord’s counterpart of the 1939 tenancy, with its Parcel B plan, passed from WGR to BP. Whether it was shown to the courts in 1955, 1962 or 1984–87 is unknown; presenting a “whole farm” tenancy while holding it would be a misstatement of fact.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Working theory: Ideal Homes transfer and woodland
x: Working theory: the Ideal Homes conveyance and plan may show where the north woodland of Parcel A passed, if overlaid on the 1955 footprint. A later purchase does not by itself show the seller's title was invalid or that the buyer knew of an earlier family interest.
src: Legal Wiki: Ideal Homes Wales — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: Cedwyn Estate Working Theory — Repeated Parcel Capture, Parcel A and the Llandough–Leckwith Land Question

t: Working theory: 1954 bid to make Frederick tenant
x: Working theory: a further attempt in 1954 to make Frederick Buckler a tenant sought to cast the Parcel A occupation as permissive. The published Court of Appeal report records instead a 10 Oct 1952 agents’ letter that the letting would not proceed. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E182 — 1954 further attempt to treat Frederick Buckler as a tenant (source pending)

t: Site ground registered as village green VG41
x: Part of the site by Leckwith Road was provisionally registered as village green VG41 on 16 June 1970 under the Commons Registration Act 1965; the current reconstruction places it within Parcel A. The VG41 ownership file records who asserted ownership of that land around 1970–80.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Parcel A as the full 1877 house estate
x: Working theory: Parcel A was the full 1877 house and quarrying estate: house, buildings, barn, stable and west-side yard, garden, north forest and the south-east ground later registered as VG41. The farmhouse and garden were only the occupied centre Mary retained.
src: Legal Wiki: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided

t: Mary refuses £2 weekly tenancy, 1965
x: On 2 March 1965 Mary refused a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at £2 offered to “Mrs Williams”; nothing was signed, no rent paid, and the estate treated her occupation as adverse from then (WGR agents' letter recited in the 1987 judgment, GHF-E009-18).

t: Eleventh-hour Strasbourg application “could not” stop demolition
x: The judge held that an application to the European Commission “at the eleventh hour” could not set up a right to “injunctive relief”, and that it would be novel to hold up the effects of a judgment until the Court of Human Rights ruled (Western Mail, 6 Dec 1988).
src: Legal Wiki: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — “Farmer fails in final eviction hearing”

t: Ownership on record years before the litigation
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement dates from about 1974, over a decade before the 1986–87 litigation. A 1974 newspaper report records her ownership position and a lawyer’s view that she had a case; William Buckler’s 1983 diary records the Daniel Thomas receipts.
src: Legal Wiki: Anticipated Objections and the Family’s Answers

t: BP public statement, April 1988: “did not appeal”
x: In April 1988 BP stated Mr Buckler had “lost the court hearing in Cardiff and did not appeal”; he had appealed to the Court of Appeal and sought House of Lords leave. Press reported Mary had “lost three previous High Court cases”; no court decided her ownership.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15 — South Wales Echo search-result extracts, April 1988 – March 1989 (index of 16 extracts)

t: Farmhouse title WA240304 applied for, Feb 1983
x: On 23 Feb 1983 Linklaters applied to register the farmhouse-and-garden title WA240304 on the May 1975 conveyance, certifying no question or doubt affecting title, while the 1974 plea of ownership by Mary (Nancy) Williams was undecided. She died on 26 March 1983.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: Manorial courts held at Great House
x: In the early nineteenth century the Bute Estate acquired the freehold of Great House, previously the Vaughan family’s chief freehold farm; the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith were held in the house (HER GGAT02038s). How Bute acquired it is unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)
Legal Wiki: Research Leads from the bpvsbuckler Archive

t: Licence letters offer farmhouse occupation, 1974
x: Letters of 31 October 1974 (addressed to “Mary Buckler” on the family copy, SOURCE PENDING; described by the Court of Appeal as to “Mrs Buckler (described again as Mrs Williams)”) offered a licence to stay in the farmhouse. The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment relied on this licence (GHF-E136; EV-0080). Whether the letters identified the land later registered to BP is not established.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: Working theory: the house was unlawfully occupied
x: Working theory: if the House Plot remained outside BP’s registered title, the 1988 possession enforcement operated against land belonging to the Williams/Buckler line, and the later control of the house was an unlawful occupation. This is an issue for counsel.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation

t: “This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down”
x: The Western Mail (20 November 1958) reported the evidence of Mary (Nancy) Buckler née Williams that the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents. She told the planning committee: “This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down.” (EV-0037).
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree
Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Licence letters: “rent free”, 31 Oct 1974
x: BP’s letters of 31 October 1974 offered Mary a licence to stay in the farmhouse; the landlords’ solicitors withdrew the warrant later, at a date before 25 November 1974. In 1988 the press reported BP’s version: “In 1974 BP Properties agreed to allow Mrs Buckler to remain in the farmhouse rent free”, “because of her ill health”.
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Clock started 1955 on an assumed tenancy
x: The Court of Appeal started the twelve-year clock on 2 February 1955, the end of Frederick’s tenancy, treating the farmhouse as part of that tenancy. Working theory: WGR’s May 1939 tenancy plan shows Parcel B only, so the farmhouse was never in that tenancy.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Museum: no record of find under dining-room floor
x: Amgueddfa Cymru refused FOI 2026-024, on a find reported under the farmhouse dining-room floor, as not held, treating records of other discoveries at the farm and at Church Farm as out of scope. The Church Farm records were later supplied under FOI 2026-036.
src: Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33-A3 — Museum Wales collections record 63.24/2: medieval iron spearhead, Llandough Church Farm, c. 1858

t: 1988 Lord Chancellor correspondence “would have been destroyed”
x: Ministry of Justice FOI 250628005 (17 Jul 2025) found only the Court of Appeal judgment; correspondence of 1988, including Alun Michael MP’s approach to the Lord Chancellor’s Department, “would have been destroyed” under retention schedules (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Only five seconds of ITV eviction coverage found
x: A five-second clip of Great House Farm survives from ITV coverage broadcast between sports programmes. The remainder of the broadcast has not been located; ITV archive, transmission records and production files would show what the unseen material contained.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: Cadw: site “not of sufficient archaeological interest”
x: In December 1988 Cadw stated the land was not of sufficient archaeological interest, though the site had been publicly identified with the early monastery of St Dochdwy and the area excavated in 1977–80. In 1994 it yielded over 1,000 early-medieval burials.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N06 — “Burnt relics represented years of digs” (South Wales Echo, 18 March 1983)

t: Farmhouse may have held 17th-century fabric
x: GGAT recorded the farmhouse as of considerable archaeological interest; though structural and documentary evidence was incomplete, it may have contained parts of a seventeenth-century building. The report notes an ownership dispute and the 1988 demolition.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: Amalgamation applied for while appeal pending
x: Two title numbers (WA231076 and WA240304) remained live after the 1986 trial, and an amalgamation application is dated 2 February 1987 while the appeal was pending (source pending: EV-0078). Two title numbers do not by themselves prove different ownership.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Limitation clock treated farmhouse as tenancy land
x: The Court of Appeal started the limitation clock in 1955 by treating the farmhouse as part of Frederick's tenancy. WGR's own May 1939 tenancy plan shows only the eastern fields (EV-0023). The judgment records the 1916 tenancy as of “the whole of the farm”.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

t: Museum Wales: “not held”, then released
x: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales twice answered requests on the 19th-century farmhouse find and farm contents with “not held”, both upheld on review; records it had already found were released only under a new request number, 57 days after the first request.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33 — Amgueddfa Cymru reply to FOI 2026-036 (5 & 7 October 2026): further collections search
Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33-A1 — Letter, Cogan Pill, 22 November 1931: spearhead, spur and skeletons found at Llandough Church Farm c. 1858 (Museum Wales file 63.24)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R33-A2 — Museum Wales collections record 63.24/1: medieval iron rowel spur, Llandough Church Farm, 1858

t: 1924 “Great House”: possibly a different farm
x: Museum Wales (7 Oct 2026) records that the “Great House” in the 1924 Llandough Estate sale particulars (MS 3360/3) was occupied by W.G. Thomas & Sons, comprised about 202 acres and lay in the Parish of Llanfair, the Llandough near Cowbridge, not this farm.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Museum places armour finds at Church Farm
x: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales replied: “It is stated that these objects were found at Church Farm, Llandough, in 1858,” resting on a letter headed Cogan Pill, 22 November 1931 (FOI 2026-036). The Museum holds nothing of a similar nature from Great House.

t: Defence counted from 1955 on “whole farm”
x: The defence counted adverse possession from the 1955 enforcement using the “whole farm” description. Working theory: this later starting point obscured the 1928 title effect and the taking of Parcel A forest and green during enforcement against Parcel B.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler
Legal Wiki: Great House Farm — The Farm / Whole Farm Nomenclature

t: Land Registrar: title “registered correctly”
x: A Land Registrar decided that “the title has been registered correctly and there are no grounds for rectification or indemnity”, closing the complaint stages, with six months to complain to the Independent Complaints Reviewer (by about 25 November 2026).

t: Land Registration Act 1925 s.115: concealment offence
x: Section 115 of the Land Registration Act 1925 made fraudulent concealment of a document or fact material to title in registration proceedings an offence. Working theory: the 1982–83 applications may engage it, a legal test to apply once the file is read.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: Llandough Farm is a separate farmstead
x: Records naming “Great House”, “Ty Mawr” or “Llandough” are not all about this farm: Llandough Farm, south of the church, was a separate farmstead on the Roman villa site, built over for housing in 1978–79; Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge is a different parish.

t: Death of William (Billy) Buckler, 1990
x: William (Billy) Buckler, born at Great House Farm on 25 August 1948, the middle one of seven children, died in 1990 at Llandough Hospital. Two dates are on record: 29 May 1990, and 29 April 1990 in the probate calendar (William Beverley Buckler of Penarth).
src: Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family
Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)

t: Working theory: 1974 steps timed before a deadline
x: Working theory: if the 1962 order reset the limitation clock, 11 Dec 1974 would have been a twelve-year deadline, and the October 1974 enforcement steps and licence letters were clustered just before it. The 1974 pleadings and judgments would test this.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: Bailiffs break in with poleaxes, Apr 1988
x: South Wales Echo, c.30 Apr 1988, “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on”: “They smashed the lock on the gate and walked round the tractor … Then they started smashing the doors with poleaxes. My children were right behind the door when the axe came through.”
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

t: Possible lack of proper care at first registration
x: Working theory: if BP or its agent applied to register the house plot despite an excluding conveyance, or without bringing the occupied plot and its occupier to the Registrar’s attention, that could have caused or contributed to a registration mistake.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: WGR offers Mary a farmhouse tenancy, 1959
x: The Court of Appeal records that in 1959 Western Ground Rents offered Mary a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden and that she refused it, asserting ownership through her grandfather (source pending: EV-0039). The original offer and reply are unlocated.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

t: BP Pension Trust conveys to BP Properties, 1975
x: On 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust conveyed land to BP Properties Ltd by a deed and plan later relied on for the farmhouse-and-garden first registration, title WA240304. The deed shows what it purported to convey, not that the transferor held every part.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake
Legal Wiki: GHF-E138 — 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust to BP Properties conveyance and plan (WA240304 items 1, 12, 13)

t: Title documents not produced in court
x: The Court of Appeal dealt with limitation and licence and recorded that the title documents relied on were not produced. The documentary title and root of title to Parcel A have not been shown to have been fully examined in the surviving court record.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: 1955 “whole farm” possession order executed
x: On 4 July 1955 a High Court possession order obtained by Western Ground Rents, described as covering the “whole farm”, was executed, including the north forest and south-east ground of Parcel A, though the dispute concerned Parcel B (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E126 — 4 July 1955 writ or warrant of possession, execution record and return
Legal Wiki: Forensic Assessment Index — Courts, Archives & Public Authorities

t: No historic conveyance supplies Parcel A's root
x: The 1982–83 first registration merged both parcels into one estate, completed by the 1987 amalgamation. Parcel B had a paper root through Bute and WGR; for Parcel A the first-registration material identifies no historic conveyance supplying the root.

t: Farmhouse largely 17th-century with earlier fabric
x: The 1994 excavation report records that the farmhouse, largely 17th-century but possibly incorporating earlier fabric, and its outbuildings stood on the site until demolition in 1988; it associates 19th-century work on the house with the Bute Estate.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence
Legal Wiki: Great House Farm — The Farm / Whole Farm Nomenclature

t: No plans found in Glamorgan Archives holdings
x: Glamorgan Archives (11 Jun 2026) identified a village sketch by Nancy Buckler (DXJF/64/30), 1938 sale particulars of unresolved site identity (DSA/6/1158) and the Western Ground Rents collection (D696), and reported no plans in the holdings searched.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R52 — Glamorgan Archives email, 11 June 2026
Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Police hold no record of 1988 evictions
x: Press reports recorded about 15 police at the 29 April 1988 stand-off and a dozen on the farm on 30 April. South Wales Police (FOI 719/26, 16 July 2026) held no information on police attendance at, or support for bailiffs at, the property, 1900–1993.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: Leave to enforce the 1962 order, 1974
x: On 19 September 1974 the county court gave BP leave to enforce the possession order of 11 December 1962, with no warrant before 31 October. Mary’s solicitors appealed because she had not been given notice; the stay application came before the judge on 4 November, and the landlords’ solicitors then withdrew the warrant, at a date before 25 November 1974.

t: ICO: no duty to create information
x: ICO letter IC-546505-W6P0 (10 August 2026) recorded that referral to other bodies and preservation of records for a legal matter were outside its remit, and that FOIA and the EIR do not require authorities to create information or give explanations.
src: Legal Wiki: Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R28-A1 — Information Commissioner’s Office letter IC-546505-W6P0, 10 August 2026

t: First-registration files: 1905, 1924, 1961 deeds
x: The WA231076 file holds a 23 February 1905 Bute conveyance granting rights to Cardiff Corporation, a 15 May 1924 agreement and a 29 March 1961 deed. The woodland register records that no copies of the 1905 plans were supplied on first registration.

t: School land conveyed, 11 June 1965
x: A conveyance of 11 June 1965 between Lakeside and Llandough Development Company Limited, Western Ground Rents Limited and Glamorgan County Council, for £16,800, carried the Llandough Primary School site. Whether the site was ever farm land is open.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Working theory: 1983 registration left out Mary’s title
x: Working theory: BP registered the house parcel in 1983 without disclosing that Mary (Nancy) Williams asserted ownership; the separate documentary root of Parcel A was never reconciled with the registered titles, and the titles were merged in 1987.
src: Legal Wiki: Fraud & Concealment — the Family’s Case

t: Burial licence lapsed, April–May 1994
x: The Home Office burial licence for the excavation lapsed from 21 April to at least 3 May 1994. What was removed in that window, and under what authority, is not established; removal without a licence was an offence under the Burial Act 1857, s.25.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: 1881 census: John Williams at “Llandough Home Farm”
x: The 1881 census records John Williams, 53, “Farmer of 170 [or 120] ac.”, with his wife Mary and children at “Llandough Home Farm”, Llandough (RG11/5288 p.2). Working theory: the census entry refers to Great House Farm under another name (EV-0224).

t: 1877 Bute–Thomas deed: no copy found
x: Glamorgan Archives holds no deeds of the 1877 sale of the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas, a Cardiff builder. A library copy of the Bute–Thomas deed was reported missing from Cardiff Library in 1984, the year of BP’s writ.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: 1938 “Great House Farm” sale was near Cowbridge
x: A 15 Nov 1938 sale of “Great House Farm, Llandough, Cowbridge”, in the parish of Llanfair, held at the Bear Hotel, Cowbridge (Glamorgan Archives DSA/6/1158), concerns a different farm near Cowbridge, not Great House Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth.
src: Legal Wiki: Excluded: not our farm (Llandough, Cowbridge)

t: Tenancy offers to Mary, 1959 and 1965
x: Western Ground Rents offered Mary tenancies of the farmhouse and garden in 1959 and 1965. The Court of Appeal’s history records that she refused the 1959 offer and that a later weekly tenancy offer was not signed or returned and no rent was paid.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: Working theory: 1983 registration notice came too late
x: Working theory: notice connected with the 1983 first registration arrived only after Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, so she never had the chance to object. The original notice and proof of dispatch are not yet found. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm: Case Overview and Key Records
Legal Wiki: GHF-E180 — Reported HMLR notification after Mary (Nancy) Williams’s death (original pending)

t: 1877 lease to John Williams not identified
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement records a lease dated 6 November 1877 to John Williams, but the matching Llandough instrument has not been identified; the physically checked DBDT/79/1 is a 2 May 1877 lease for Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff (SC-20).
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: RCAHMW post-demolition visit undocumented
x: RCAHMW record NMR 6048945 is Richard Suggett’s one-page post-demolition record. RCAHMW holds no record of the date or purpose of the visit beyond the catalogue entry; a 29 September 2026 reply confirmed the visit took place after the demolition.

t: Heritage record classed “POST MEDIEVAL – Farm”
x: The Historic Environment Record entry GGAT02038s is headed and classified “POST MEDIEVAL – Farm”, although its own source file records possible medieval fabric, reported medieval ironwork and the site’s historic setting beside the parish church.

t: LRA 1925 ss.115–116: suppression in registration
x: The Land Registration Act 1925 contained express provisions on suppression of documents or facts in registration proceedings (s.115) and fraudulent procurement of register entries (s.116), the historical legal test for the 1982–84 registrations.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review Addendum — 6 October 2026 Fresh Reassessment

t: RCAHMW: “no correspondence”, then a lost file
x: On 28 May 2026 RCAHMW wrote “we do not hold any correspondence related to the site”; on 10 June it reported that archive 6048945 carries the note “Correspondence between C.N. Johns and Mrs Buckler, Great House Farm, has been lost since 1986/87”.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Northern forest: permissive framing, then 1961 deed
x: Working theory: in 1949 occupation of the northern forest was cast as permissive while Mary (Nancy) Williams asserted ownership; about twelve years later a deed of 29 March 1961 created a paper estate over it. The deed and plan are not yet read.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: Judgment: Mary “conceived the notion” of ancestral title
x: The 1987 judgment describes Mary as having “conceived the notion” of ancestral title and records that she did not produce the documents. The published reasons do not establish whether the 1877 transaction vested Parcel A in the Williams family.
src: Legal Wiki: Court of Appeal — Forensic Assessment

t: Bute serves notice to quit, 1877
x: Mary's statement records that Bute served notice to quit in 1877, then sold the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres to Daniel Thomas while keeping about 9 acres “up on the top”; her grandfather then held each part from a different landlord.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

t: Human Rights Commission rules application inadmissible
x: In 1989 the European Commission of Human Rights accepted that the possession order interfered with William Buckler’s home, his home since birth, but held it lawful and justified and declared the application inadmissible (GHF-E027-09; EV-0122).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler
Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family

t: Annexes missing from 1989–90 planning file
x: The 1989–90 planning material for application 89/01396/OUT lacks annexes (Appendices B–E) referred to in the officer’s report. Some submissions are understood to have given reasons against demolition of the historic farmhouse (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry
Legal Wiki: Redevelopment and Church View Close

t: 1955 order and execution papers unseen
x: The originals of the 1955 possession order and the 4 July 1955 execution papers, and any parcel plan, have not been obtained (GHF-E125, E126); the events are known only through later references. The 1962 pleadings and plan are likewise unseen.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive
Legal Wiki: GHF-E125 — 1955 High Court Order 14 possession order against Frederick Buckler, with particulars, affidavits and any plan
Legal Wiki: GHF-E126 — 4 July 1955 writ or warrant of possession, execution record and return

t: Interest passes to BP Pension Trust, then BP Properties (our case: Parcel B and an interest in the 1962 order on Parcel A in 1969)
x: Later instruments recite a 31 Dec 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust. A 23 May 1975 conveyance from BP Pension Trust to BP Properties is linked with the farmhouse title WA240304. The exact parcels are not yet proved.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: 1924 Bute–Corbett drain agreement on the file
x: HM Land Registry holds a record dated 15 May 1924 between John, Marquis of Bute and James Pelham Stuart Corbett that “relates to the construction and maintenance of a drain”. It is recorded as an agreement, not a conveyance (WA231076 item 2).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Working theory: undisclosed evidence in 1984–87 litigation
x: Working theory: if the 1984–87 litigation file shows BP held material evidence inconsistent with the case it put to the court and did not disclose it, in circumstances amounting to fraud, a Takhar ground to set aside the 1987 judgment arises.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: Leave to appeal to House of Lords refused
x: The 1987 Court of Appeal report records: “Leave to appeal to the House of Lords was refused but a stay pending a possible application to the House was granted on terms.” A petition for leave to the House of Lords followed (EV-0080, GHF-E142).
src: Legal Wiki: House of Lords — Forensic Assessment

t: 1877 lease to John Williams not located
x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams quotes an 1877 lease to John Williams of the Llandough land. That instrument has not been found; Glamorgan Archives’ DBDT/79/1, examined on 14 Sep 2026, is a different counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Possessory case for rest of farm failed
x: The Court of Appeal noted that the possessory-title case for the remainder of the farm had failed at first instance, the acts relied on being found too tenuous and equivocal, and that part of the possession order was not challenged on appeal.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: Appeal argued Mary held as owner, not licensee
x: At the appeal hearing of 16–17 July 1987 it was argued that Mary never accepted the 1974 licence because she regarded herself as owner. The court held the 1962 action was in time and the 1974 letters made her possession permissive (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Llandough manor to Bute line, 1767–1793
x: In 1767 the manors of Dinas Powis, Landough East and Cogan were held by William Hurst and Calvert Richard Jones; Llandough followed Cogan, bought by the Earl of Bute in 1793. This does not show Great House Farm passed in the same instrument.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

t: 1997 Act removes six-year indemnity bar
x: Section 83(11) of the Land Registration Act 1925 set a special six-year period from registration for some indemnity applications. Section 2 of the Land Registration Act 1997 substituted a new section 83 without that registration-date limit.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

t: Villagers and a councillor condemn demolition
x: Between 7 and 13 December 1988 a Vale councillor and BP pensioner called the demolition “disgusting”, and Llandough villagers met councillors. William Buckler, bailed, told the press: “All I’ve got left are the clothes I stand up in” (N15).

t: Registry indemnity time runs from knowledge
x: Under Land Registration Act 2002 Schedule 8 paragraph 8, time for an indemnity application runs from when the applicant knew, or might have known, of the grounds. The April 1983 registration correspondence was first identified in July 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Working theory: repeated “permissive” framing of Mary
x: Working theory: repeated efforts to present Mary (Nancy) Williams’s occupation as permissive (1949, 1959, 1965, 1974), alongside later dealings affecting the woodland and the VG41 ground, weakened or obscured the title to the full Parcel A.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

t: 1983 certificate: “no question or doubt” on title
x: Linklaters applied for the farmhouse title WA240304 on 23 February 1983 and certified they knew of no question or doubt affecting title, though Mary's 1974 plea of ownership had never been decided. Working theory: this omission is material.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Mary pleads ownership; BP revives 1962 order
x: BP Pension Trust sued Mary in 1974; on 3 July 1974 the action was adjourned part heard for a defence, which pleaded the Limitation Act 1939. The action stalled and BP revived the 1962 order instead. Licence letters followed on 31 October 1974, one from BP Properties, which then held only a contract to buy.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Mary died in occupation, never a tenant
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams died at the farmhouse on 26 March 1983 in occupation of the house parcel (Parcel A), never having signed a tenancy or accepted the licence; the date is also given in the European Commission's decision of 14 April 1989.

t: 1824 survey: “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”
x: Stewart's 1824 survey of the Bute estates, plan 19, records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”: 139a 3r 8p including 20a 2r 35p of wood; tenant read as John Gedrick; 10a 3r 39p of “late Thos. Williams” land added (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1; EV-0211).

t: Thomas tenancy with “special provisions”
x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams reads: “Daniel Thomas required the farm for quarrying limestone and I remember seeing the tenancy agreement between D. Thomas and my grandfather which contained special provisions with regard to this.”

t: “Might have been different” limited to licence point
x: The 1987 appeal judgment’s remark that the result might have been different concerned Mary expressly repudiating the 1974 licence letters. It is not a finding that a full trial of the 1877 root title would have produced a different result.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Fraud requires proof of conscious dishonesty
x: Deceit, or setting aside a judgment for fraud, requires proof of conscious dishonesty judged by the standards of honest people (Ivey v Genting Casinos [2017] UKSC 67). Negligence, muddle, lost files and changing explanations are not fraud.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Actual occupation overrides on registration
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams was in actual occupation when WA240304 was applied for in 1983. Under s.70(1)(g) Land Registration Act 1925 any proprietary right of hers bound BP on registration (compare Malory v Cheshire Homes [2002] EWCA Civ 151).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Court of Appeal leaves rectification open, 1987
x: Dillon LJ stated that if Mary had acquired a valid title to the farmhouse and garden, it would have been an overriding interest binding BP’s registration, and her personal representatives would be entitled to seek rectification (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

t: Press: Mary “fought and lost” three cases
x: The South Wales Echo of 29 April 1988 reported that Mary had “fought and lost three previous High Court cases” over ownership. The court record shows no case in which her ownership was decided; the 1955 action was against Frederick alone.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Forest of Cardiff: woodland bought after due diligence
x: Forest of Cardiff stated in correspondence that it bought the woodland from Ideal Homes (now Persimmon Homes) after due diligence, sold a small western section about 20 years ago, and has proposed a private sale of the remaining woodland.
src: Legal Wiki: Forest of Cardiff — Forensic Assessment

t: Council silent on 1982 records and photographs
x: Llandough Community Council's 11 October 2026 response did not separately state search outcomes for photographs or records of the 1982 transfer and deposit of its minutes, nor explain how the environmental-information aspect was assessed.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough Community Council — Correspondence Chronology

t: Possession of “the whole of the farm”
x: The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment records: “Western Ground Rents then brought proceedings for possession against Mr Frederick Buckler in the High Court and obtained a possession order, under Order 14, in respect of the whole of the farm.”
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Working theory: a reconstructed “whole farm” parcel
x: Working theory: a later document or composite parcel was used to reconstruct a “whole farm” description without the genuine documentary chain for the house plot. To be proved or disproved from the conveyances, plans and register history.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: Taking title deeds was a felony in 1950
x: Taking documents of title to land was a felony under the Larceny Act 1916 (s.7), and knowingly receiving them a separate offence. The Limitation Act 1939 (s.26) already postponed limitation where a right of action was concealed by fraud.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: First registrations WA231076 and WA240304, 1982–83
x: First registration of title WA231076 was applied for on 30 Nov 1982 and of WA240304, the farmhouse title, on 23 Feb 1983. The files hold correspondence of April and May 1983, after Mary’s death, and a new register edition of 13 Jan 1984.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: Mary’s papers and journal lost in eviction
x: Possessions including Mary’s papers, photographs and journal were left in the house or thrown into the road during the November 1988 eviction (source pending). William Buckler put the loss at about £30,000 (South Wales Echo, 1989; N13).
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Land Registry points to paid statutory routes
x: HM Land Registry (FOI F260213) confirmed it holds recorded information about land on the north side of Leckwith Road, Llandough, but withheld it under FOI as available through the statutory routes of public inspection, which carry fees.
src: Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: Agreement dated 15 May 1924 on WA231076
x: Title WA231076 lists “Agreement dated 15 May 1924”, parties not given. Working theory: it may connect with the 1928 freehold split recalled by Mary (Nancy) Williams; other readings treat it as a Bute–Corbett drain agreement. Unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Land Registry rejects registration complaint citing 1987
x: In 2026 HM Land Registry cited the 1987 judgment when rejecting the complaint about the 1982–83 registration, although the registration was a distinct earlier event and the full Parcel A extent was not decided in the possession appeal.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: No document shows how Parcel A was acquired
x: The registration narrative treats the conveyances as covering the farm as one holding. Western Ground Rents acquired Bute's fields (Parcel B) in 1938, but no document on file shows how it or BP acquired the farmhouse parcel (Parcel A).
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

t: Leases of “Cydfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, 1552–1824
x: National Library of Wales Bute Estate Records D 219, Llandough manorial leases 1552–1829, include leases of “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)” in the parish of Llandough, dating from 1552 to 1824 (D219/1, D219/4–5, D219/8 onward).
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

t: 1877 notice to quit from the Bute Estate
x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams reads: “Prior to 1877 my Grandfather held the farm as tenant of the Bute Family Estates and in that year he received notice to quit from the Bute Estate Office. … he showed me the notice to quit.”
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Llandough manor passes to the Herberts, 1543–45
x: Henry VIII granted Llandough manor in 1543 to Lord Clynton and Say and Robert Turwitt; by 1545 Sir George Herbert held it, as a rent-roll shows, and he appears to have conveyed it to his grandson Sir William Herbert (Cardiff Records).
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

t: “Reputed to be 800 years old”, 1988
x: Western Mail, 6 Dec 1988, “Farmer fails in final eviction hearing”: Janet Harris stated the house had been in the family for four generations. “It is reputed to be 800 years old and yet it seems they can destroy it on what is a whim.”
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N10 — “Farmer fails in final eviction hearing” (Western Mail, 6 December 1988)

t: 1938 conveyance passed only the Parcel B reversion
x: Working theory: the 1938 conveyance to Western Ground Rents (WGR) transferred the reversion of the earlier agricultural tenancy, and the 1939 plan shows the fields east of the farmhouse rather than Parcel A (source pending: EV-0019).
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy
Legal Wiki: GHF-E118 — February 1916 Bute yearly tenancy to John Williams, with plan
Legal Wiki: GHF-E121 — 1938 Bute–Western Ground Rents conveyance and plan

t: “The woman takes on the husband’s name”
x: HM Land Registry’s stage-two decision (25 May 2026) answered the objection to the description “Mrs Buckler”: on marriage “the woman takes on the husband’s name”; “It is the identity of the person that matters not which name is used”.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Weekly tenancy offered to “Mrs Williams”, 1965
x: On 2 March 1965 the agents of Western Ground Rents offered “Mrs Williams” a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at £2. It was not signed or returned and no rent was paid; the estate treated her occupation as adverse from then.

t: Possession order is not a freehold conveyance
x: The 1955 and 1962 possession orders bear on possession, pleadings and occupation. A possession order is not, merely by being made, a conveyance of the freehold; the land covered and legal effect of each order are separate questions.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

t: Conveyances to BP Pension Trust and BP Properties
x: Between 1969 and 1975 Western Ground Rents conveyed to BP Pension Trust, and BP Pension Trust to BP Properties, describing the land together. The 1969 root deed and the 1971 abstract are absent from HM Land Registry’s 2026 schedule.

t: Conveyance of 19 Nov 1982 behind WA231076
x: HM Land Registry’s registration history records that the first registration of WA231076 (applied for 30 November 1982) relied on a conveyance dated 19 November 1982, and WA240304 (23 February 1983) on a conveyance dated 23 May 1975.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: Bailiffs evict the Bucklers, 30 Nov 1988
x: On 30 November 1988 the South Wales Echo front page ran “Angry scenes as farmer evicted”. Bailiffs who forced entry had already removed half the roof of one outbuilding, and Branwen feared BP would flatten the farmhouse (N14, N15).

t: Cadw cannot produce its spot-listing file
x: Cadw can produce two photographs but not the assessment file, inspector notes, decision record, decision-maker’s identity, correspondence, transfer record or destruction record for the 1988 spot-listing consideration (ATISN 27021).
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: Occupier’s rights bind every later buyer
x: Under the doctrine of notice (Hunt v Luck, 1902) anyone acquiring land was fixed with notice of the rights of the person in actual occupation. From 1926, Land Registration Act 1925 s.70(1)(g) made those rights overriding interests.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1974 survey noted historic features, possible medieval core
x: The regional Historic Environment Record entry GGAT02038s cites R. F. Suggett’s December 1988 note and H. J. Thomas’s 1974 survey of the house, which recorded historic architectural features and considered a possible medieval core.
src: Legal Wiki: European Commission of Human Rights / Strasbourg — Forensic Assessment

t: Royal Commission: full search, nothing withheld
x: The Royal Commission (RCAHMW, RC26-0375) recorded that its searches covered registered files, the National Monuments Record archive by subject and by area, and a manual search of uncatalogued material, and that nothing is withheld.
src: Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: First registration of main site, Nov 1982
x: First registration of the main site, title WA231076, was applied for on 30 November 1982; the title is now registered to Persimmon Homes (Wales) Ltd. The instrument carrying the farmhouse and garden into it has not been identified.

t: Ogee-stopped beam found in the rubble
x: Richard Suggett of RCAHMW visited briefly after the demolition in December 1988; the reason is not recorded. The HER text records: “Examination of the rubble brought to light no new features except an ogee-stopped beam with torus”.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree
Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: BP: rent-free “because of her ill health”
x: In 1974 BP stated it allowed Mary to stay rent-free “because of her ill health”; she was a widow and an amputee in a wheelchair. The Court of Appeal held the letters made her possession permissive although she never accepted them.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Stolen chattels are not time-barred
x: Limitation Act 1980 s.4: no limitation period runs for a stolen chattel, except against a later good-faith purchaser. Working theory: if the 1950–52 family papers or the 1988 house contents were stolen, ownership of them survives.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: Leckwith Woods given to Cardiff Corporation, 1940–42
x: In 1940–42 Western Ground Rents gave Leckwith Woods, “110 acres of wooded land at Leckwith”, to Cardiff Corporation (EV-0220); the deed and plan are pending. The measured outline lies 0 ha in Llandough, 1.25 km from the farmstead.
src: Legal Wiki: Woodland & Land-Transfer Assessment 1902–2005 (parcel identity)

t: 1916 tenancy recited as the “whole farm”
x: In February 1916 the Marquess of Bute granted John Williams a yearly agricultural tenancy that the judicial history describes as concerning the “whole farm”. The 1939 revised tenancy’s surveyed plan shows only the eastern fields.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: 1969 root deed and 1971 abstract missing
x: Later documents recite a 31 Dec 1969 conveyance from Western Ground Rents to BP Pension Trust and a 1971 abstract of title, but HM Land Registry’s 30 July 2026 schedule does not list either as surviving on the registration files.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: Working theory: a gap became a title fact
x: Working theory: a gap in the documentary chain to Parcel A was converted into an apparent title fact by registration and by repeated later description. Whether that was accidental, negligent, misleading or fraudulent is unproved.
src: Legal Wiki: Fresh Paradigm — Independent Cross-Review of Evidence, Fraud, Concealment & Public Authority Lines (6 October 2026)

t: Penarth estate agent and 1951–52 conviction
x: Working theory: the loss of the title papers c.1951–52 is linked to Mr Knapp, a Penarth estate agent and lay preacher, and to the conviction of Bruce Sutherland in that period; identities and connections are being traced (A-080).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Cadw officers note high roof beams, 1988
x: Before Cadw's 5 December 1988 decision, Cadw officers entered the house and carried out a survey, remarking on the height of the roof beams (witness statement of Branwen, 19 October 2026; EV-0255). Inspection date source pending.
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Farmhouse opened to the public, 1974
x: On 15 April 1974 Mary (Nancy) Williams, then 60, opened the farmhouse “to show what the nation is losing”, and hundreds came. About 1,000 people had signed a petition. “My family has lived here for more than 400 years” (EV-0048).

t: Solicitors certify “no question or doubt” on title
x: At first registration BP’s solicitors, Linklaters, certified that they knew of “no question or doubt affecting the title”. Mary had pleaded ownership and limitation in court in 1974, and that plea was never withdrawn or decided.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Judgment: BP owned “the whole” farm since 1982
x: The published judgment states that BP had paper title and had been registered proprietor of “the whole” farm since November 1982, while two separate titles (WA231076 and WA240304) were live until the 1987 amalgamation (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: Court of Appeal — Forensic Assessment

t: Bute granted “a slice of land”, Leckwith Common
x: Western Mail, 7 May 1958, p.7, reported Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler of Great House Farm at the Leckwith Common inquiry: about 130 years earlier Lord Bute allowed her family “a slice of land” which was now Leckwith Common (EV-0035).
src: Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

t: 1876 poor rate: farm owned by Lord Bute
x: The Llandough poor rate of October 1876 records John Williams rated for a farm of about 76 acres, owner Lord Bute; Lord Bute for woods in hand, 32a 3r 39p; Daniel Thomas & Son for a lime kiln and quarry (provisional; EV-0212).

t: Woodland excised to Goldsworthy Homes, 2005
x: In 2005 land was excised from the Forest of Cardiff woodland title WA735527 and passed to Goldsworthy Homes (EV-0139); the charity’s accounts record land at Leckwith Road sold for £20k (EV-0217). The deed and plan are pending.
src: Legal Wiki: Woodland & Land-Transfer Assessment 1902–2005 (parcel identity)

t: Working theory: part of a wider Cedwyn estate
x: Working theory: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr belonged to a wider historic Cedwyn/Cydfin estate across Llandough and Leckwith, and successive land transactions, possession events and registrations took it apart parcel by parcel.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr): The Williams–Buckler Dispute
Legal Wiki: Cedwyn Estate Working Theory — Repeated Parcel Capture, Parcel A and the Llandough–Leckwith Land Question

t: Vale authorises legal action against BP, 1989
x: South Wales Echo, 11 Feb 1989, p.2, reported that the Vale of Glamorgan Council authorised legal action against BP Properties after a 13 December 1988 letter went unanswered, and that an enforcement notice was being prepared.
src: Legal Wiki: Press and Archive Leads — October 2026

t: House and farm buildings destroyed, 6 Dec 1988
x: RCAHMW archive 6048945 records: “The house and farm buildings were suddenly and completely destroyed by B. P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988”. The press chronology dates the outbuildings’ demolition to 30 November 1988.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: 1938 sale may have scattered Bute records
x: The National Archives (3 Mar 2026) described the 1938 “sale of the estate’s leasehold interest to the Western Ground Rents Company”, which “led to the widespread dispersal and possibly destruction of the Bute estate records”.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: St Dochdwy’s churchyard may date to 7th century
x: GGAT recorded that the church of St Dochdwy and its surroundings are of considerable archaeological interest, the churchyard likely on the site of an earlier foundation perhaps dating to the seventh century AD (Davies 1978).
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: 1924 Llandough Estate sale was near Cowbridge
x: The 9 Oct 1924 Llandough Estate sale, including Lot 3 “Great House” (D/DSA6/701), covered the “Parishes of Llanfair and St. Hilary” near Cowbridge, vendor Sidney H. Byass. It is not Great House Farm, Llandough-juxta-Penarth.
src: Legal Wiki: Excluded: not our farm (Llandough, Cowbridge)

t: 1905 conveyance likely concerns Parcel B
x: The 1905 Bute conveyance appears to concern rights over land Bute retained and may relate to Parcel B. The 15 May 1924 Bute–Corbett drain agreement may or may not touch Parcel A; neither deed nor plan has yet been inspected.

t: Spur, spearhead and burials at Church Farm, c.1858
x: The Museum's 1931 letter records a spur and spearhead found at “Llandough Church Farm” about 1858, with about six skeletons reburied south of the church. Whether Church Farm was part of the Great House holding is unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Injunction to stop demolition refused, Dec 1988
x: Western Mail, 6 Dec 1988: after a hearing in chambers a judge at Cardiff dismissed the application of Mr and Mrs Buckler for an injunction restraining BP Properties Ltd from destroying or damaging the fabric of the building.
src: Legal Wiki: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — “Farmer fails in final eviction hearing”

t: 1877 arrangement placed house estate with Thomas/Williams
x: Working theory: the 1877 arrangement placed the full house and quarrying estate on the Thomas/Williams side and took effect in 1928, so WGR’s 1938 reversion covered only the remaining eastern agricultural fields (Parcel B).
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

t: Outline planning consent with archaeology condition
x: The Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council granted outline planning consent on condition that “no development shall take place until a field evaluation survey and archaeological assessment report has” been completed (GGAT 1990).
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: House of Lords papers on BP v Buckler
x: The National Archives identified House of Lords judicial papers for BP Properties Ltd v Buckler (YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536, item 19, container HL/PO/JO/10/11/2536). The series was released to its online catalogue on 20 May 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: Physical inspection request unanswered
x: By 25 September 2026 the request of 3 June 2026 to inspect the historic registration files physically remained unanswered in substance, and a formal non-destruction confirmation beyond “will remain on file” was outstanding.

t: Injunction: “a small victory”, 30 Nov 1988
x: An ITV Cymru Wales report of 30 Nov 1988 on the eviction and possession enforcement showed Branwen with her arm in a sling, presented as having won a small victory through an injunction and hoping the judge would uphold it.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E113 — ITV Cymru Wales report: Great House Farm, eviction / possession enforcement and injunction

t: House of Lords leave to appeal refused
x: Western Mail, 6 Dec 1988, reported that the Bucklers had unsuccessfully sought leave to appeal to the House of Lords, an Appeal Committee ruling they had exhausted the remedies available under the laws of England and Wales.
src: Legal Wiki: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — “Farmer fails in final eviction hearing”

t: County court possession order for farmhouse, 1962
x: On 11 December 1962 the county court made a possession order for the farmhouse and garden against Frederick and Mary, the remaining occupied house group within Parcel A. The Court of Appeal later treated it as enforceable.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Licence offered before BP Properties held title
x: The first 31 October 1974 letter, from BP Pension Trust, recorded an agreed sale to BP Properties; the second, from BP Properties, offered the licence. BP Properties did not take a conveyance until May 1975 (court record).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: GGAT advised, priced, then was commissioned
x: In one 1989–90 document GGAT advised the regulator, specified the method, priced the work (£2,000) and disclosed negotiations with BP, and was then commissioned. Separation of functions has never been shown (T4–T5; A-043).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: 1916 tenancy describes “the whole farm”
x: The 1916 Bute tenancy to John Williams described the holding as the whole farm, treating house and fields as one; later records (the 1955 order, conveyances, the 1982 registration and the 1987 judgment) repeat the wording.

t: Possible gap in the chain to Parcel A
x: Working theory: if the 1938 conveyance did not include Parcel A and no other instrument conveyed it to Western Ground Rents, the December 1969 deed to BP Pension Trust would carry a material gap in the chain for Parcel A.
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

t: Working theory: limitation complete by 1940
x: The twelve-year period for recovery of land already existed under section 1 of the Real Property Limitation Act 1874. Working theory: if rent and acknowledgement ended in 1928, a twelve-year period would have run by 1940.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

t: 1955 possession order against Frederick Buckler
x: Frederick Buckler’s tenancy was ended by notice on 2 Feb 1955. The High Court then made an Order 14 summary order against him alone for “the whole of the farm”, enforced on 4 July 1955 except for the farmhouse and garden.

t: Local Plan: retain buildings; no preservation notice
x: The East Vale Local Plan (February 1987) stated the buildings on the site should be retained. The Council had power to serve a building preservation notice (Town and Country Planning Act 1971, s.58); no notice was served.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Stephen Doughty MP's office makes enquiries
x: In August 2026 the office of Stephen Doughty MP, after apologising for earlier unanswered correspondence, made enquiries on the matter and on 18 September 2026 forwarded a response from HM Land Registry's Chief Executive.
src: Legal Wiki: Office of Stephen Doughty MP — Forensic Assessment

t: 1972 housing permission missing from council search
x: The 1989 officer’s report records a housing permission of 25 July 1972, and a 1974 report cites permission for about 13 houses; the Vale council’s 2026 search “from 1875 onwards” found only the 1989 and 1992 applications.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: 1992 approval adds no archaeology condition
x: Reserved matters (92/00671/RES) were approved on 3 September 1992 with no new archaeological condition, 38 days after GGAT’s letter of 27 July 1992 reported significant deposits including human bone and urged mitigation.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: No grant of representation to Mary's estate
x: The 1987 Court of Appeal report records that no grant of representation to the estate of Mary (Nancy) Williams had been obtained by July 1987. Solicitors: Loosemores for Mr Buckler; Linklaters & Paines for BP Properties.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review Addendum — 6 October 2026 Fresh Reassessment
Legal Wiki: FOI & Records Requests — Backstory, Status and Forward Plan
Legal Wiki: GHF-E141 — 31 July 1987 Court of Appeal judgment: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2

t: Northern forest and green seized, 1955
x: Working theory: the 1955 enforcement against the fields of Parcel B also took two parts of Parcel A — the forest north of the house and the ground south-east of it later registered as village green VG41 (source pending).

t: Demolition and clearance removed the house floors
x: GGAT’s 1990 Trench 7 found that only features cut into the clay and lias substrate survived; any floor levels of the north-west part of Great House Farm had been removed during the 1988 demolition or the 1989 clearance.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: Rent-free stay framed as “ill health”
x: A BP spokesman stated in April 1988 that Mary was allowed to live there rent-free “because of her ill health”. The 1974 letters followed directly on an undecided ownership plea and a revived possession order (N07, N15).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N15 — South Wales Echo search-result extracts, April 1988 – March 1989 (index of 16 extracts)

t: Two separate first-registration strands
x: The land entered the register in two strands: WA231076, the earlier strand for the fields (Parcel B), and WA240304, the later farmhouse-and-garden strand relying on the 23 May 1975 conveyance (source pending: EV-0052).
src: Legal Wiki: 1983 First Registration: Parcel A Title Basis and HMLR Mistake

t: A failed 1954 attempt cannot restart limitation
x: A failed attempt in 1954 to make occupation permissive would not, merely by being proposed, restart a limitation period already completed. The legal effect of the 1955 and 1962 possession orders is a separate question.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Daniel Thomas buys farmhouse, lets to Williams
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s statement records that in 1877 Daniel Thomas bought the farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres from Bute and let them to her grandfather. The original instrument and plan have not been located.
src: Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

t: NLW leases of Cydfin or Ty Mawr Farm
x: The National Library of Wales holds D219 leases of “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm”, a 107-acre holding, 1552–1824. NLW noted Ty Mawr translates as Large House or Great House; the identity with this farm is not yet shown.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: 1962 order on a “one farm” premise
x: Working theory: the 1962 order depended on the farm being one unit as in 1916; the 1924/1928 Parcel A freehold split, the 1938 conveyance and the 1939 tenancy were not, so far as the record shows, put before the court.
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

t: Long silence over land outside the house
x: Long non-challenge over land outside the occupied house can be read against the family as lack of possession, an accepted boundary or acquiescence. Silence does not transfer ownership, but nor does it preserve a title.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: Press: BP let Mrs Buckler stay rent free
x: The South Wales Echo of 29 April 1988 reported that Mary had fought and lost three previous High Court cases and that “in 1974 BP Properties agreed to allow Mrs Buckler to remain in the farmhouse rent free” (EV-0088).
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Local Plan called for retention; buildings demolished
x: The adopted East Vale Local Plan Policy H.2 stated the farm buildings should be retained, yet they were demolished before the housing application was determined. No record yet shows how the Council reconciled the two.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: ITV Wales films eviction aftermath, 1988
x: An ITV Cymru Wales report recorded the aftermath of the 1988 possession enforcement at Great House Farm, the injunction, BP’s position, a reference to the site as development land, and Branwen with her arm in a sling.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: GHF-E113 — ITV Cymru Wales report: Great House Farm, eviction / possession enforcement and injunction

t: Linklaters letters on registration files, 1983
x: The HM Land Registry file schedule records multiple Linklaters & Paines letters, including correspondence of 12 May 1983, connected with titles WA240304 and WA231076. Linklaters acted for BP in the 1984–87 litigation.

t: 1941–43 National Farm Survey form not yet seen
x: The 1941–43 National Farm Survey Penarth parish bundle (TNA MAF 32/1220/39), which would generally record occupier, owner and water supply, has not been seen; Great House Farm's form is inferred to be in it (EV-0241).

t: Court of Appeal: “whole” farm, registered proprietor
x: The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment described Bute’s 1916 grant as an agricultural tenancy of the “whole” farm, the 1938 reversion as conveyed to Western Ground Rents, and BP as registered proprietor from November 1982.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: Two dates for the 1975 conveyance plan
x: HM Land Registry file WA240304 lists item 13 as a “Plan to conveyance dated 23 February 1975”, while item 1 and every other record give 23 May 1975. Whether this is a typing slip or a second instrument is unresolved.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1877 terms rest on childhood memory
x: The 1877 terms rest on Mary's memory of a document she saw as a child, and the account of papers being taken is second-hand. Her statement was made c.1974, before the litigation, and the 1974 press record matches it.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

t: Working theory: woods gift took Parcel A woodland
x: Working theory: the 1940 gift of “110 acres of wooded land at Leckwith” to Cardiff (Western Mail, 14 Sep 1940, p.5) took in the woodland third of Parcel A, now held by the Forest of Cardiff charity on title WA735527.
src: Legal Wiki: Woodland & Land-Transfer Assessment 1902–2005 (parcel identity)

t: 1939 tenancy plan shows Parcel B only
x: The plan attached to the 1939 tenancy shows the land let as Parcel B, the fields east of the house, not the farmhouse plot (Parcel A). The plan is held. Read beside the WGR grazing-let square, which cuts against it.
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

t: Returned deeds are not proof of concealment
x: HM Land Registry normally returned original deeds and abstracts to applicants after first registration, so the absence of the 1969 conveyance and 1971 abstract from the file is not by itself evidence of concealment.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1980: Trust excavates at Llandough
x: The Neath Guardian of 17 April 1980 reported a talk by the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust’s assistant director on its work, including excavations at Llandough near Cardiff, in the separate Roman-villa context.
src: Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N05 — 17 April 1980: “Historical Society had notable year” (Neath Guardian)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N05 — “Historical Society had notable year” (Neath Guardian, 17 April 1980)

t: Record losses cluster around proceedings
x: Working theory: losses of records cluster around legal proceedings: c.1950–52 before the 1955 action, 1984 at the writ, and 1986/87 at trial and appeal. Explanations are being sought from the record-holders (A-078).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: “From farm to a bus”, 1989
x: South Wales Echo, 1989, “From farm to a bus” by Peter Collins: “They have taken everything from me and my family. I have lost my livelihood.” The report recorded £30,000 of possessions taken from the site (EV-0112).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N13 — “From farm to a bus” (South Wales Echo, 1989)

t: “Bulldozed Before Breakfast”: farmhouse demolished
x: On 6 December 1988 a twenty-strong team with bulldozers moved in just after 4am; by breakfast no building was left standing. Branwen and the three children watched (N11; Echo headline “Bulldozed Before Breakfast”).

t: Statement: last rent to Alfred Thomas, 1928
x: Mary's statement: machinery remained at the quarry “until 1928 when the machinery was removed and the last payment of rent was made to Alfred Thomas the son of Daniel Thomas”, paid by her father at about £4 a year.

t: Forest of Cardiff holds woodland title WA735527
x: On 25 Sep 2026 the Forest of Cardiff charity’s company secretary wrote that the charity bought the woodland on title WA735527 and offered a route to ownership; the offer was not accepted and the title did not pass.

t: 19th-century Bute estate work on Great House
x: The archaeological report associates 19th-century work on Great House with the Bute Estate; H. S. Corbett, a Bute-associated agent, remodelled Baron's Court around 1850. His role at Great House is not established.
src: Legal Wiki: Llandough (Penarth) — Cydfin / Tŷ Mawr and Pre-1877 Manorial Evidence

t: Working theory: 1938 deed carried “whole farm” forward
x: Working theory: the drafting of the 1938 bulk sale to Western Ground Rents carried “whole farm” wording forward, so later records treated Parcel A and Parcel B as one. The 1938 deed and 1939 plan would test this.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: Archaeology condition discharged over Trust objection
x: In 1993–94 planning Condition 18 was treated as discharged on the developer’s counsel’s opinion over the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust’s objection, which the Council described as a “difference of opinion”.
src: Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
