Legal Wiki: GHF-E148 — 1994 Cotswold Archaeology report, Condition 18 discharge and the developer’s counsel’s opinion

t: 1974 licence letters: possession recast as licence
x: BP letters dated 31 Oct 1974, covering the central house and garden, were later treated by the Court of Appeal as placing Mary’s continued possession under a licence, which was material to the limitation outcome.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr): The Williams–Buckler Dispute

t: Wales Office holds no Great House Farm records
x: On 22 Sep 2026 the Wales Office answered FOI 26FOI 103: it “does not hold the information requested”; any paper files of the former Welsh Office on the matter would have been transferred to The National Archives.

t: HMLR unaware of the occupier’s interest
x: HM Land Registry’s stage-two decision (25 May 2026) stated it had not been aware at first registration of the occupying family’s interest or of a possibly ongoing dispute, and declined rectification or indemnity.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: John Williams succeeds father in tenancy, 1855
x: The Cardiff Times (16 July 1904) reported that John Williams “succeeded his father in the tenancy of the farm in 1855”, calling him “of Llandough Farm”; identification with Great House is an inference (EV-0224).

t: Post Office holds no record of Mr Williams
x: In July 2026 Post Office Limited stated that it did not hold records of a Mr Williams of the Cardiff Post Office Engineering Department and his part in Marconi’s 1897 Lavernock Point experiments (FOI2026/00751).
src: Legal Wiki: Post Office Limited — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: Later good-faith buyers are protected
x: Limitation Act 1980 s.32(3) protects a later purchaser for valuable consideration who was not party to any fraud, as does the priority rule for registered land. This bears on any remedy concerning the woodland.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1974 H. J. Thomas architectural survey
x: RCAHMW holds the H. J. Thomas survey material for Great House Farm, including a 1974 architectural survey and floor plan documenting a sub-medieval / late-seventeenth-century building, with related photographs.

t: 1974 licence letter from a not-yet-owner
x: The second letter of 31 Oct 1974 came from BP Properties, which held only a contract to buy until the May 1975 conveyance, after BP Pension Trust’s action stalled on the ownership plea of Mary (Nancy) Williams.
src: Legal Wiki: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-074 to A-087)

t: Frederick’s 1949 letting; no 1949 offer to Mary found
x: In 1949 Frederick took a new yearly agricultural tenancy from 2 February (Court of Appeal 1987, para 5); the written agreement that was intended was never made. No 1949 offer to Mary concerning Parcel A, or reply from her, has been found; the offer of a tenancy of the farmhouse that the judgment records, which she refused, is undated and comes after 1955. In April 1974 she told the Daily Telegraph that ownership had been “in dispute for 25 years”.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Tenancies from Bute and Thomas; death 1908
x: After the 1877 sale the grandfather of Mary (Nancy) Williams took tenancies from both Bute and Daniel Thomas, the Thomas tenancy providing for the freehold to pass to him when quarrying ended. He died in 1908.
src: Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family
Legal Wiki: Daniel Thomas and Alfred Thomas

t: House only partly recorded before demolition
x: The regional Historic Environment Record notes the building was completely demolished on 6 Dec 1988 and that the structure had only been partly recorded because of problems arising from the ownership dispute.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: 1994 cemetery finds donated by Ideal Homes
x: Objects found in land belong to the landowner (Waverley BC v Fletcher [1996] QB 334). The 1994 cemetery assemblage from the site was donated to the Museum by Ideal Homes Wales as landowner (accession 95.56H).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: September 1974 enforcement order
x: A September 1974 enforcement order was made against the occupation. Mary (Nancy) Williams’s solicitors challenged it on notice grounds; the appeal notice, order and outcome are not yet seen (source pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: “No such documents were, however, ever produced”
x: The appeal judgment records of Mary’s title papers: “No such documents were, however, ever produced.” Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c. 1974 statement records that the title deed and papers went missing in 1950–52.
src: Legal Wiki: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

t: Farmhouse and barn rejected for listing, 1988
x: Cadw’s listed-buildings casework stated on 21 May 2026 that the farmhouse and barn were assessed and rejected in the 1988 Llandough community survey, and supplied no other electronic records of the decision.
src: Legal Wiki: Cadw — Forensic Assessment v8.0.0 (full text)
Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: Bailiffs remove the family; house later demolished
x: In late November 1988 BP’s enforcement agents and bailiffs entered Great House Farm and removed the occupying family. Injunction proceedings followed, and the farmhouse was demolished in early December 1988.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation

t: Statement: lodger placed at farm, June 1950
x: Mary's statement records that in June 1950 Mr Knapp, a Penarth estate agent and lay preacher, asked her mother to give accommodation to a man; the man was later imprisoned for theft and told never to return.

t: Suggett records features in the rubble
x: In December 1988 R. F. Suggett of RCAHMW examined the rubble and recorded a fireplace jamb, an ogee-stopped beam with torus, and the loss of the carved stone capital kept by the front door (HER GGAT02038s).
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)

t: BP Pension Fund sells 1,300 Welsh acres
x: In October–November 1988 the BP Pension Fund sold about 1,300 acres of Welsh land to Intercontinental Land & Development (Cardiff) Ltd for £29,375,400; the farm site stayed with BP Properties Ltd (EV-0270).

t: No plan in the woodland chain is held
x: Not one plan in the woodland chain — 1902 auction, 1938 conveyance, 1940–42 gift, 1969 conveyance, 1994 transfer, 2005 excision — is yet held, so every link between these records rests on description alone.
src: Legal Wiki: Woodland & Land-Transfer Assessment 1902–2005 (parcel identity)

t: Court and ministerial records of 1988 still unseen
x: Not yet seen: the court record of the 1988 interim injunction and of the 5 December hearing, magistrates’ court records for 1988–89, and Alun Michael’s correspondence with the Lord Chancellor’s Department.

t: CPR 52.30: reopening a final appeal
x: CPR 52.30 allows a final appeal determination to be reopened where necessary to avoid real injustice, the circumstances are exceptional and there is no alternative effective remedy; permission is required.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review Addendum — 6 October 2026 Fresh Reassessment

t: Working theory: adverse possession against WGR by c.1951
x: Working theory: if the 1939 plan shows WGR's tenancy covered only the fields, adverse possession of the house parcel against WGR from 1938–39 would have completed about 1951, before the 1955 order (A-077).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Village sketch by Mrs Nancy Buckler, c.1945–55
x: A note and sketch of the old village layout by Mrs Nancy Buckler of Great House Farm names her father as John Williams of Great House Farm, “born about 1867” (Glamorgan Archives D/D XJF 64/30–31; EV-0155).

t: HM Land Registry refuses rectification and indemnity
x: HM Land Registry found “no evidence of a mistake in the register” (23 Mar 2026), and its stage-two complaint decision (25 May 2026) held the land “registered correctly”, with no rectification or indemnity.

t: 1982–83 title: no root for Parcel A
x: Working theory: BP’s 1982–83 registration merged both parcels into a title with no documentary root for Parcel A, resting on failed attempts to make the occupation of Mary (Nancy) Williams look permissive.
src: Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family

t: WGR sues Frederick alone, “whole of the farm”
x: In 1955 Western Ground Rents sued Frederick Buckler alone in the High Court by summary judgment (Order 14) on his tenancy, using the words “the whole of the farm”. Mary was not a party to the 1955 action.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 29 April 1988 enforcement attempt fails
x: On 29 April 1988 bailiffs and police attended Great House Farm to enforce possession; the drive was blocked and, after a stand-off involving a chainsaw, the attempt ended without the family being removed.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

t: Working theory: 1949 recasting of occupation as permissive
x: Working theory: the 1949 tenancy was the first later attempt to make Mary’s occupation of Parcel A appear permissive despite the 1928 title effect; it preceded the loss of the title deed. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Great House Farm Working Reconstruction (6 October 2026)

t: Working theory: title documents never before the courts
x: Working theory: the documents that decide title to the house parcel, the 1877 agreement, the 1938 conveyance and plan and the 1939 tenancy, were never put before the courts in 1955, 1962, 1974 or 1986–87.
src: Legal Wiki: Fraud & Concealment — the Family’s Case

t: John Williams takes over farm on father's death
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement records: “In the year 1908 my grandfather died and my father took over the farm.” Her grandfather had held tenancies from both Bute and Daniel Thomas since the 1877 sale.

t: 1958 development plan inquiry record unread
x: Days 20–24 of the 1958 public local inquiry into the Glamorgan County Council Development Plan (Area No. 2), 19 November – 11 December 1958, are recorded verbatim at TNA BD 28/177; not yet read (EV-0239).

t: ECHR application declared inadmissible, 1989
x: The application of William (Billy) Buckler to the European Commission of Human Rights (14464/88), under Articles 6, 8, 13 and Article 1 of Protocol 1, was declared inadmissible on 14 April 1989 (EV-0122).
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E145 — European Commission of Human Rights application 14464/88 and the 14 April 1989 inadmissibility decision

t: Outbuildings then farmhouse demolished; rubble cleared 1989
x: The outbuildings were demolished on 30 November and the farmhouse on 5–6 December 1988, dates the press corroborates. Lorries began clearing the rubble at 7.30am on 20 March 1989 (South Wales Echo; N15).

t: Vale Council finds records after “nothing in scope”
x: On 7 July 2026 the Vale of Glamorgan Council replied that no additional information had been identified within scope; on 11 September 2026 it replied that further historical documentation had been found.
src: Legal Wiki: Anomalies Register — Lines of Enquiry

t: Broadcast clip omits pregnancy and infant children
x: The surviving clip of the 1988 report does not mention that the mother was pregnant or that three infant children lived at the farm. Whether the original broadcast included this has not been established.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment

t: 1971 abstract of title missing from file
x: HM Land Registry (19 Apr 2026) stated that an abstract of title dated 1971 “was lodged with the application for first registration”; its 30 July 2026 schedule of 43 file documents lists no such abstract.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Development assessed at Tŷ Mawr Farm, 1982
x: HER record GGAT02038s records an October 1982 GGAT assessment and consultation concerning Tŷ Mawr Farm (H2.1) and archaeological investigation before development, while the farmhouse was still occupied.

t: 1987 judgment did not try title
x: The 1987 judgment decided limitation and licence, not who owned Parcel A; it did not try title. Later decisions, including HM Land Registry’s 2026 complaint decisions, rely on it as if it settled title.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Police: no record of bailiff support, 1900–1993
x: South Wales Police (FOI 719/26) replied that it holds no information on police attendance at, or support for bailiffs at, Great House Farm between 1900 and 1993. An internal review (1188/26) was opened.
src: Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: Surviving ITV clip is a later copy
x: The viewing copy of the HTV report (GHF-E113) carries an “itv CYMRU WALES” identifier, a brand first used in 2014. The original transmission, its duration and its edit history have not been established.
src: Legal Wiki: ITV Cymru Wales (formerly HTV Wales) — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E113 — ITV Cymru Wales report: Great House Farm, eviction / possession enforcement and injunction

t: 1969 root conveyance absent from HMLR files
x: On 30 July 2026 HM Land Registry supplied the schedule of 43 documents surviving on the first-registration files. The 31 December 1969 root conveyance and the free-standing 1971 abstract are not listed.

t: WGR conveys to BP Pension Trust, 1969
x: In 1969 Western Ground Rents conveyed its interest to BP Pension Trust. The conveyance has not been retrieved; the 1987 judgment treats the sale as including the farmhouse and garden (EV-0043, pending).

t: Farm agreement and title deed go missing
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams stated that papers including the farm agreement were removed from the farmhouse blanket box in 1950–52 and that the title deed was found missing. Who removed them is not recorded.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: Title documents “never produced” in 1987
x: The 1987 court recorded that Mary's title documents were “never produced”, without knowing why. Mary (Nancy) Williams stated in her c.1974 witness statement that they were taken in 1950–52 (F1; A-058).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights
Legal Wiki: Testimony — Mary (Nancy) Williams (Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler, 1913–1983)

t: 1916 tenancy of “the whole of the farm”
x: The 1916 tenancy is recited as of “the whole of the farm”, and its scope covered both areas; if Bute let the house in 1916, Bute still owned it. The 1939 revised tenancy covers the eastern fields only.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: 1974 licence letters covered house and garden only
x: The 1974 licence letters applied to the farmhouse and garden. Working theory: a ruling on those letters does not decide the woodland or the green land, if a separate documentary title to them is shown.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: Page 2 of GGAT’s 1992 warning letter missing
x: On 27 July 1992 GGAT warned the Council that significant archaeological deposits including human bone existed on the site and urged mitigation. Page 2 of the letter is missing from the surviving file.

t: HER classifies the site “POST MEDIEVAL – Farm”
x: Historic Environment Record GGAT02038s is classified “POST MEDIEVAL – Farm” for Great House Farm, while describing a historic site beside the parish church with medieval pottery and ironwork recorded.

t: DCMS holds nothing on the farm’s movable heritage
x: On 22 July 2026 DCMS replied to FOI2026/06174, on furniture, furnishings and heirlooms from the farm, that no information is held; internal review IR2026/06711 upheld the nil return on 19 August 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E106-R29-A1 — DCMS FOI2026/06174 response, 22 July 2026

t: HMLR support: title “closed in 2005”
x: On 21 September 2026 an HM Land Registry support agent stated the title was “closed in 2005”, conflicting with the registry's own chronology of first registrations in 1982–83 and amalgamation in 1987.

t: Possession taken except farmhouse and garden, 1955
x: The 1987 judgment records that on 4 July 1955 possession was taken of all parts except the farmhouse and garden, an exception attributed to Mary’s recent return from hospital and her strong objection.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: GGAT played no part in demolition or listing
x: GGAT did not demolish the farmhouse, did not advise its demolition and had no part in the decision not to list it. From December 1993 to December 1994 its documented conduct defended the archaeology.

t: 1953 payments may count as acknowledgments
x: Working theory (opposing argument): Frederick Buckler’s 1953 rent and mesne-profit payments may be argued as acknowledgments of the landlord’s title; the land they related to has not been identified.
src: Legal Wiki: Fresh Paradigm — Independent Cross-Review of Evidence, Fraud, Concealment & Public Authority Lines (6 October 2026)

t: Linklaters–HMLR correspondence after Mary's death
x: On 8 and 12 April 1983 Linklaters and HM Land Registry corresponded on the farmhouse title WA240304, including form D23 “inside exam”, after Mary (Nancy) Williams's death (EV-0069, EV-0070, pending).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1994 excavation: over 1,000 burials
x: The 1994 excavation at Llandough recorded 858 inhumations in the preliminary report; the later publication reported 1,026 burials investigated. Whether the burials lay on Parcel A has not been shown.
src: Legal Wiki: Master Scrutiny Issue Register — Public, Court & Institutional Handling

t: BP serves writ on William Buckler, 1984
x: After Mary died on 26 March 1983, her son William Buckler inherited her estate and stayed at the farm. On 22 May 1984 BP served him with a writ for possession of Great House Farm and adjoining land.
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler
Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family
Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)

t: “Low potential” zone held burials, 1994
x: Eight machine trenches were dug; ground that “could not be investigated” was nonetheless zoned low potential, and the 1994 excavation found burials there, many just below the topsoil (T6–T7; A-045).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: House only partly recorded due to dispute
x: RCAHMW recorded that the house was only partly recorded “because of problems created by an ownership dispute”, and that the Johns–Buckler correspondence has been lost “since 1986/87” (A-035, A-036).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Farm and barn rejected for listing, 1988
x: Cadw’s 1988 listed-buildings survey assessed Great House Farm and its barn and rejected both for listing. Two photographs dated 29 July 1988 survive, coded “YYY”, meaning “marginally below the bar”.

t: Register can be rectified for mistake
x: Under Schedule 4 of the Land Registration Act 2002 the register can be rectified to correct a mistake. When BP first registered in 1982–83, the occupiers were in actual occupation of the farmhouse.
src: Legal Wiki: Anticipated Objections and the Family’s Answers

t: Mary repeatedly refused to be a tenant
x: The Court of Appeal’s 1987 account supports that Mary refused the 1959 tenancy offer and asserted ownership; she repeatedly rejected being treated as a tenant and maintained that she was the owner.
src: Legal Wiki: Repeated attempts to frame Mary (Nancy) Williams’s Parcel A occupation as permissive

t: Strasbourg case file destroyed under retention policy
x: The underlying file of European Commission of Human Rights application 14464/88 was destroyed under the Court’s retention policy; the application number, decision date and archive metadata survive.
src: Legal Wiki: European Court of Human Rights / ECHR Archives — Forensic Assessment

t: Titles amalgamated during the appeal, 1987
x: An application to amalgamate the registered titles was made on 2 Feb 1987, while the appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler was live. Its exact legal and spatial effect is unproved. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: Welsh Office files moved 1999 and 2007
x: The Wales Office recorded that paper files went to the National Assembly for Wales in 1999 and to the Welsh Government in 2007, while Cadw and RCAHMW responses describe different custody positions.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: Welsh Office / Wales Office — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: Welsh Government — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: The National Archives — Forensic Assessment

t: Surrendered tenancy concerned the fields only
x: The farming, the arrears and the surrendered tenancy all concerned the fields held under the 1939 tenancy (Parcel B). Working theory: John Williams held no tenancy of the house parcel to surrender.

t: Complaints Reviewer declines to intervene, 2026
x: On 9 October 2026 the Independent Complaints Reviewer declined to substitute its view for HM Land Registry’s registration decision and took a broad view of the significance of the 1987 proceedings.
src: Legal Wiki: Three Parts of Parcel A — Divergent Chronologies before 1987 Amalgamation

t: Deposits older than the farm buildings survive
x: GGAT’s 1990 trial trenches found that, outside the quarried area, archaeological deposits pre-dating the farm buildings, presumed built in the nineteenth century for the Bute Estate, had survived.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: 1989 report: farmhouse a “county treasure”
x: GGAT’s 1989 planning report described the farmhouse “as having been listed as a ‘county treasure’”. Cadw records that the house was not a designated asset and “did not meet the listing criteria”.
src: Legal Wiki: Source Conflicts Register — Where Public-Authority Replies and the Wiki Disagree

t: Tenancy “intended” for Frederick, never written
x: The appellate record reads: “It was intended that Mr Frederick Buckler should have a written tenancy agreement, but this did not happen because Mr Frederick Buckler also failed to pay the rent.”
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Planning report’s appendices B–E missing
x: The Vale planning officer’s report on application 89/01396/OUT refers to appendices B–E, which are missing from the surviving record; Appendix B held further archaeology comments from the Trust.
src: Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E146 — 1989 planning officer’s report 89/01396/OUT (appendices B–E missing) and the 13 March 1990 outline permission

t: Rent to Alfred Thomas ends, 1928
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c. 1974 witness statement records the last rent paid to Alfred Thomas in 1928, and that she paid no rent to, and acknowledged the title of, no other landlord thereafter.
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

t: Court of Appeal dismisses appeal, 31 Jul 1987
x: On 31 July 1987 the Court of Appeal (Dillon LJ, with Mustill LJ and Sir Edward Eveleigh agreeing) gave judgment for BP Properties Ltd in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080).
src: Legal Wiki: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal

t: GGAT advised both planners and BP
x: The 1990 GGAT report records that BP Properties commissioned the work and that GGAT “played a dual role”, advising the Local Planning Authority and providing comparable advice to the applicant.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: “reputed to be the stable of a Castle”
x: An RCAHMW note records that the house “was reputed to be the stable of a Castle, which could be verified by the finding of the remains of a soldier in armour, his horse, lance” and other items.

t: Court finds a tenancy without written agreement
x: The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment concluded that “even though there was no written agreement, Mr Frederick Buckler had a periodic tenancy which was protected by the Agricultural Holdings Act.”

t: Post-demolition planning and archaeology, 1990–94
x: A 1990 GGAT Great House Farmhouse assessment, 1992 approval material and a 1994 Cotswold Archaeology Llandough report document post-demolition planning and archaeological handling of the site.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)
Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)

t: HER records site as “Post Medieval – Farm”
x: The historic environment record leads with “Post Medieval – Farm”, holds the cemetery in a separate linked record, and carries the 1994 burial figure (858) without the published 1,026 (T11.2).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Jim Driscoll’s first fight in the farm barn
x: A secondary local-history summary records that the boxer Jim Driscoll (“Peerless Jim”) had his first fight in a barn at Great House Farm, Llandough. The year is not recorded. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr): The Williams–Buckler Dispute

t: Open-ended land right exposed to perpetuities rule
x: A right to land arising on an uncertain future event with no time limit was vulnerable to the rule against perpetuities as against later owners (London & South Western Railway v Gomm, 1882).
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: 1939 tenancy plan shows Parcel B only
x: The May 1939 agreement between Western Ground Rents and John Williams, with its plan, depicts Parcel B only, the eastern agricultural fields, although later records use “whole farm” wording.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: Museum Wales 1931 letter and medieval artefacts
x: A letter dated 22 November 1931 linked to Museum Wales file 63.24, with collection records for a medieval rowel spur and spearhead, provides artefact-provenance leads for the Llandough area.
src: Legal Wiki: Institutional Involvement Roadmap — Chronology of Actors, Decisions and Evidence (1877–2026)

t: Limitation largely expired; s.32 needs concealment
x: Most limitation periods expired long ago; s.32 Limitation Act 1980 needs proof of deliberate concealment, not just loss. Time runs from discovery, and many key records surfaced only in 2026.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: High Court judgment for BP, 24 July 1986
x: After a hearing on 10 July 1986 before Hollis J, the High Court gave judgment for BP on 24 July 1986, suspending possession for six months (South Wales Echo, 25 July 1986; EV-0074, pending).
src: Legal Wiki: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler

t: Limitation against WGR complete about 1951
x: Working theory: any adverse possession of the house against Western Ground Rents ran from 1938–39, not 1955, and would have completed about 1951, before the 1955 order and long before 1962.
src: Legal Wiki: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions (October 2026)

t: Frederick joins Mary at the farmhouse, 1936
x: Mary (Nancy) Williams stated that after their 1936 marriage Frederick Buckler “came to live with me at the Farmhouse”. They had seven children, among them William (Billy), the middle child.

t: 1952: landlords’ agents drop the letting
x: The 1987 judgment records “a letter from the landlords’ agents to their solicitors of October 10 1952 stating that they did not propose to proceed with the letting to Mr Frederick Buckler.”

t: Photograph of the half-demolished farmhouse
x: A David Purser Photography black-and-white image shows the partially demolished Great House Farm farmhouse, with St Dochdwy’s church tower behind, taken during the December 1988 demolition.
src: Legal Wiki: GHF-E170 — David Purser Photography: Great House Farm ruins with St Dochdwy church, c.1988

t: Evicted family lives with relatives, plans bus home
x: In 1989 William, Branwen and their children lived with his sister in Penarth, and he planned to convert an old bus into a home (South Wales Echo, “From farm to a bus”, Peter Collins; N13).
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Strasbourg ruling leaves new-evidence route open
x: The 1989 inadmissibility decision of the European Commission of Human Rights was made on the 1988 record, without the title documents. It does not bar domestic proceedings on new evidence.
src: Legal Wiki: Anticipated Objections and the Family’s Answers

t: Wales Office: paper files moved, digital search only
x: The Wales Office answered FOI 26FOI 103 from a digital search only; its response letter recorded that paper files went to the National Assembly in 1999 and to the Welsh Government in 2007.
src: Legal Wiki: FOI & Public-Authority Reply Register — every reply email and its attachments

t: Woodland title passes to Forest of Cardiff
x: Registered woodland title WA735527 was transferred to Forest of Cardiff on 10 Nov 1994 and altered by an excision in 2005. How it overlays the historic Parcel A woodland is not yet mapped.
src: Legal Wiki: Forensic Master Chronology — Authoritative Corrected Version (6 October 2026)

t: No sign earlier surveys were considered
x: Cadw could not confirm whether the 1974 RCAHMW survey, the Sites and Monuments Record, GGAT's 1978–80 work or the 1982 warning were considered in its 1988 assessment (Cadw report VII.2–3).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: 1949 re-grant used to frame occupation permissive
x: Working theory: the 1949 agricultural tenancy re-grant concerned Parcel B and was the first attempt to make Mary's separate Parcel A occupation appear permissive (EV-0025, source pending).

t: Eviction attempt fails, 29 April 1988
x: On 29 April 1988 an eviction attempt failed: the drive was blocked by a tractor, doors were axed, and William held the bailiffs off with a chainsaw; the bailiffs withdrew after four hours.
src: Legal Wiki: Event Nomenclature Register — 1988 Great House Farm removal, seizure and occupation
Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Parcel B: “does not concern this action”
x: The statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams records that the “about 9 acres up on the top” retained by the Bute Estate in 1877 (Parcel B) “was given up later, and does not concern this action”.
src: Legal Wiki: 1938–39: Sale to WGR and the Revised Tenancy

t: Cadw assesses the farmhouse for listing, 1988
x: Cadw’s 2026 disclosure record shows the farmhouse was visited and assessed for listing in 1988. Two Cadw photographs dated 29 July 1988 survive (ATISN 27021; internal review 2 July 2026).

t: 1982 warning on the farm’s archaeological sensitivity
x: On 1 Oct 1982 the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust wrote a letter warning of Great House Farm’s archaeological sensitivity. The recipient and any reply are not known. (source pending)
src: Legal Wiki: GGAT — Forensic Assessment and Evidence Schedule v4.0.3 (full text)
Legal Wiki: GHF-E139 — 1 October 1982 GGAT warning about Great House Farm

t: Williams connection to the house since 1667
x: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr) stood beside St Dochdwy’s Church, Llandough-juxta-Penarth. Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c.1974 statement traces the family’s connection to the home to at least 1667.
src: Legal Wiki: Great House Farm: Case Overview and Key Records
Legal Wiki: Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr)
Legal Wiki: The Williams / Buckler Family

t: Pwll-y-Pant Williams estate left to Bute, 1870
x: William Evans Williams of Pwll-y-Pant, Caerphilly, a different Williams, died in February 1870 and left his estate to the Marquess of Bute; the 1870 probate of his will is at NLW D242/17.

t: Bute's “Cwm Cydfin Wood” offered at auction, 1902
x: On 29 November 1902 the Marquess of Bute's coppice woods, including “Cwm Cydfin Wood, Leckwith and Llandough”, were offered at auction by Stephenson & Alexander (particular 192; EV-0219).

t: Mary opens farmhouse to the public, 1974
x: On 15 April 1974 Mary (Nancy) Williams opened the farmhouse to the public “to show what the nation is losing”; a petition gathered about 1,000 signatures (Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974).
src: Legal Wiki: Press Archive — Newspaper Transcripts

t: Notice of registration after Mary’s death
x: Working theory: notice of the registration reached the occupying family only after Mary (Nancy) Williams died on 26 March 1983, leaving her no practical window to object (source pending).

t: Press: “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on”
x: A newspaper report headed “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” was published around 30 April 1988, during the dispute over the trees and the possession order at Tŷ Mawr (Great House Farm).
src: Legal Wiki: Home Office — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E090-N07 — “Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on” (c. 30 April 1988)

t: 1949 surrender and new tenancy to Frederick Buckler
x: John Williams fell into arrears; his tenancy was surrendered and “a new yearly agricultural tenancy commencing at February 2 1949” was to be granted to his son-in-law, Frederick Buckler.

t: Working theory: title never tried in 1984–87
x: Working theory: in the 1984–87 litigation Mary's ownership case was set aside and the defence narrowed to adverse possession, leaving ownership of the house parcel untried (§2.1; A-076).
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Homes bid on Great House Farm land, 1990
x: The South Wales Echo (23 February 1990) reported a homes bid on the Great House Farm land on its front page; the Community Council made no objection but wanted a village green (EV-0273).

t: Adverse-possession defence at High Court, 1986
x: In the High Court action BP v Buckler (hearing 10 July 1986, judgment 24 July 1986), William (Billy) Buckler defended on adverse possession (EV-0074). The trial judgment is not yet held.

t: Outline permission for housing, 13 Mar 1990
x: The 1989 planning officer’s report on application 89/01396/OUT led to outline permission for housing on the site on 13 March 1990; appendices B–E of the report are missing from the file.
src: Legal Wiki: Vale of Glamorgan Council — Forensic Assessment
Legal Wiki: GHF-E146 — 1989 planning officer’s report 89/01396/OUT (appendices B–E missing) and the 13 March 1990 outline permission

t: BP’s agents open redevelopment talks after demolition
x: Following the December 1988 demolition, GGAT entered discussions with Debenham Tewson, agents for the site owners BP Properties Ltd, on the archaeological implications of redevelopment.
src: Legal Wiki: 1990 GGAT Archaeological Assessment — Land at Great House Farm, Llandough — Transcription

t: WGR had to prove its own paper title
x: Working theory: against Mary as an owner-claimant in 1962, Western Ground Rents had to prove its own paper title to Parcel A rather than rely on Frederick’s ended tenancy of the fields.

t: 1955 order: Mary not made a party
x: The 1955 possession order was obtained by summary judgment against Frederick Buckler alone, although Mary (Nancy) Williams, who asserted title, lived in the house. She was not a party.
src: Legal Wiki: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights

t: Bute conveys its reversion to Western Ground Rents
